## What

Builds the visible, policy-controlled browser session UI on top of what is on `develop` today (the `/api/browser-bridge` sessions/settings/confirm routes and the plugin-browser policy helpers):

- **`BrowserSessionPolicyPanel`** (`packages/ui/src/components/browser/BrowserSessionPolicyPanel.tsx`) — lists the agent's bridge sessions with:
  - the effective **domain-mode verdict** per session domain (granted / blocked / all-sites / current-site-only / outside grants / paused / control off / bridge disabled / unresolved), rendered as an accent (orange) or danger badge;
  - **user takeover**: approve/decline controls for `awaiting_confirmation` sessions via `POST /api/browser-bridge/sessions/:id/confirm`;
  - **domain modes**: per-domain grant / block / unblock controls writing `grantedOrigins`/`blockedOrigins` via `POST /api/browser-bridge/settings`;
  - **submit interception**: sessions surface their held steps (explicit `requiresConfirmation`, and account-affecting/submit steps when `requireConfirmationForAccountAffecting` is on);
  - **session TTL**: finished sessions show their retention deadline and are hidden once expired (24h default);
  - **receipts**: finished sessions render their result as a receipt with unconditional redaction of credential-looking keys (token/secret/password/cookie/authorization/…) — no cookie export, no rehosting, ever.
  - Loading, designed-empty, and error are three distinct states with a retry affordance; the clock lives in an effect (never read in render) so renders stay deterministic.
- **`browser-session-policy.ts`** — pure policy math: fail-closed domain-mode resolution ordering (disabled → paused → blocklist → allow modes), origin normalization (`https://x/*`, `*.x`, ports/paths) and subdomain matching, interception selection, TTL expiry, receipt redaction/truncation.
- **`client-browser-bridge.ts`** — typed `ElizaClient` extension over the existing bridge routes (`listBrowserBridgeSessions`, `getBrowserBridgeSettings`, `updateBrowserBridgeSettings`, `confirmBrowserBridgeSession`), registered in `api/client.ts`.
- Storybook stories for empty / load-error / awaiting-takeover / blocked+outside-grants / finished-with-receipt states (story-gate coverage).

## Tests

- `browser-session-policy.test.ts` — 16 deterministic unit tests: disabled/paused pre-emption, blocklist-beats-all_sites, granted vs outside grants, subdomain vs suffix-fragment matching, unresolved-domain fail-closed, interception on/off, TTL anchor (finishedAt vs updatedAt), bad-timestamp tolerance, redaction (including nested objects) and truncation.
- `BrowserSessionPolicyPanel.test.tsx` — 8 jsdom behaviour tests driven through a protocol-faithful in-memory transport (confirm flips awaiting→queued/cancelled; settings writes merge like the route): loading→empty, error→retry→ready, per-domain verdict rendering, approve and decline takeover, grant then block a domain, intercepted-step + redacted-receipt rendering (secret value never in DOM), action-error banner on a failed write.

## What

Derives — rather than predesigns — the reusable managed-provider adapter SDK from the existing plugin-maps JSON adapter, and lands it in `@elizaos/core` under `src/integrations/managed-provider/` (exported from the root Node surface):

- **Connection resolver** (`connection.ts`): explicit `managed` (opaque `conn_*` Cloud connection id + gateway origin, no credential ever present at the runtime) vs `local`/BYO (explicit endpoint + user credential) modes. Strict validation of provider ids, opaque connection ids, and origin-only endpoints; **no silent fallback** between modes. Local connections get a deterministic opaque audit handle that never embeds the endpoint or credential.
- **Typed HTTP client** (`http-client.ts`): SSRF-guarded (core `fetchWithSsrfGuard`, DNS-pinned, redirects rejected), origin-pinned, deadline-bounded, byte-limited JSON transport with schema-validated decoding (structural `safeParse` seam, no zod dependency in core) and a designed-null 404 path (`requestOptionalJson`).
- **Failure taxonomy** (`errors.ts`): `ManagedProviderError` with stable codes (auth expired/revoked, rate limited + `retryAfterMs`, timeout, network, endpoint blocked, oversize, malformed, rejected/failure, pagination overflow) and `toCapabilityExecutionErrorCode` mapping onto the #19878 capability execution contract.
- **Pagination** (`pagination.ts`): `collectProviderPages` with page/item ceilings and repeated/empty-cursor rejection so a hostile upstream cannot loop the runtime.
- **Health** (`health.ts`): non-throwing `probeProviderHealth` producing typed snapshots (`healthy` / `reauth_required` / `revoked` / `rate_limited` / `unreachable` / `degraded`) for catalog/kill-switch and Connections surfaces (#19887/#19884).

## Reference migration

`plugins/plugin-maps/src/adapter.ts` is rewritten on top of the SDK (−580/+120 lines of transport code): the SDK owns transport, deadlines, bounded reads, and classification; the plugin keeps the maps route contract, provider-spoofing assertions, and translates the shared taxonomy into `MapsError` codes at its boundary. Managed mode (no credential) and local/BYO mode (credential) both go through `resolveProviderConnection`. The plugin's full existing suite — including `test/provider-contract.test.ts`, which drives the real HTTP adapter against the #19909 protocol-faithful fake upstream — passes unchanged, proving behavior parity. Local mode has no runtime Cloud dependency; the SDK lives in `@elizaos/core` (ESM, project references).

## Tests

- New deterministic suite `packages/core/src/integrations/managed-provider/managed-provider.test.ts` (17 tests) over injected transports: success, designed-empty and designed-null, invalid input (ids/endpoints/limits), pagination (drain, loops, overflows), expired/revoked auth, rate limiting with retry-after, malformed/contract-drift/oversize bodies without leaking provider bytes, timeouts, private/blocked origin rejection, bearer/connection-id header propagation.

## What

Adds a provider-neutral normalized finance capability layer to `@elizaos/plugin-finances`, with freshness/calculation metadata on reads and receipts on internal writes. Read/derive only — nothing implies payments or trading.

**New module `src/finance-capabilities.ts`** (pure, deterministic, no I/O):
- `computeSourceBalances` — per-source ledger-derived net flow (credits minus settled debits). Pending rows are excluded from settled figures and reported separately; every observed currency is surfaced instead of silently merged; metadata explicitly states balances are transaction-derived, not institution-reported.
- `computeBudgetStatus` — user-supplied budget vs settled debit spend in a rolling window (`under_budget` / `near_limit` / `over_budget`), with pending/credit/out-of-window rows excluded and counted.
- `detectAnomalies` — possible duplicate charges (same source/merchant/amount within 3 days) and amount spikes (>= 2.5x a merchant's average over 3+ prior charges, >= $20 delta). Uses the normalized merchant name so adversarial raw strings ("NETFLlX.COM*8873") group with their real merchant; pending rows never generate anomalies.
- `normalizeSubscriptions` — regular-cadence recurring charges (confidence >= 0.5) projected into provider-neutral subscription records.
- `buildCapabilityMeta` — `FinanceCapabilityMeta` on every capability response: `generatedAt`, freshness (`latestDataAt` of consumed rows, counts), and calculation provenance (`derived_from_transactions` | `provider_reported` | `user_supplied_input`, window, notes).
- `buildWriteReceipt` — `FinanceWriteReceipt` (id, capability, operation, entity, occurredAt, outcome, counts) with no credentials or row payloads.

**Action surface (`src/actions/finances.ts`)**: four new OWNER_FINANCES subactions — `balances`, `budget_status` (requires `budgetUsd`, rejects missing/non-positive), `subscriptions`, `anomalies` — and receipts attached to the existing internal writes (`add_source`, `remove_source`, `import_csv`; the CSV receipt is only issued when state actually changed). All exported from the package barrel; docs (CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md/README) updated.

## Tests

- `src/finance-capabilities.test.ts` — 17 deterministic unit tests over the pure layer: multi-account, multi-currency, pending rows, duplicate/near-duplicate/cross-source negatives, adversarial merchant strings, thin-history spike suppression, empty ledgers, receipt shape/uniqueness, strict pending-flag typing.
- `test/finances.real-db.test.ts` — 4 new real-PGLite integration tests driving `runPaymentsHandler` end to end: write receipts on add/remove source, derived balances + freshness metadata from real rows, budget_status invalid-input + over-budget evaluation, and a real duplicate-charge anomaly plus designed-empty subscriptions.

## What this does

Projects all managed connections into the shared connected-capability API without merging their storage tables, on top of the provider-neutral `ConnectedAccount` contract merged for #19878 (PR #22643).

- **Projection service** (`packages/cloud/shared/src/lib/services/connected-capabilities/`): maps four storage families — cloud OAuth credentials (`platform_credentials`), vendor OAuth connections (`vendor_connections`), Discord connector accounts (`discord_connections`), and native phone-gateway devices (`phone_gateway_devices`) — into contract-normalized `ConnectedAccount` DTOs via the real `normalizeConnectedAccount` from `@elizaos/core`. Storage tables stay separate; the DB loader reads each with an org-scoped SQL filter.
- **Opaque handles, no secrets**: account IDs are `ca_<sha256-derived>` digests of source family + row ID — never credential row IDs. The projection never reads token/ciphertext/DEK/nonce columns; tests assert the serialized payload contains no secret material, email, phone number, or row UUID.
- **Status / last-used / capabilities**: credential lifecycle states map onto contract statuses (`connected`, `reauth_required`, `revoked`, `error`, `disabled`, `unavailable`); granted OAuth scopes project to per-capability risk levels (mutating scopes R2, reads R1); phone-gateway native permission booleans project as capabilities, with ungranted permissions surfaced as `unsupported` rather than hidden.
- **API**: `GET /api/v1/connections/accounts` (offset pagination via the shared fail-closed parser, `providerId`/`mode` filters) and `GET /api/v1/connections/accounts/:accountId` (detail; cross-org and unknown handles 404, malformed handles 400). Mounted ahead of the legacy `/connections/:platform` param route.
- **Worker bundle**: the Workers `@elizaos/core` shim re-exports the pure provider-integration contract pieces from real core source so the Worker runs the actual normalizer, not a stub.
- **Cloud SDK**: regenerated public-route surface adds `getApiV1ConnectionsAccounts` / `getApiV1ConnectionsAccountsByAccountId`, plus mirrored `ConnectedAccount*Dto` types.

## Scope notes

- Local/self-hosted BYO-credential runtimes have no cloud-persisted connection state today; the contract's `local` mode is already served by the enum and the projection's source-loader seam, so a local source registers without an API change when one lands (per the #19877 architecture, local mode never silently falls back to Cloud).
- Rate limiting rides the API-wide middleware; the routes add no per-route override.

## Tests and gates

- `packages/cloud/shared` — 13 new deterministic contract tests over the real projection/service (success, designed-empty, revoked/error/reauth, malformed upstream scopes, soft deletes, pagination totals, cross-org handle isolation, handle stability, fail-closed loader): **13 pass**.
- `packages/cloud/api` — 10 new Hono route tests running the live handlers against a real `ConnectedCapabilitiesService` over typed rows (defaults, pagination, invalid limit/offset/provider/mode, provider filter, empty org, 401, structured 500 without storage context, detail 200/404/400): **10 pass**.
- `packages/cloud/sdk` — full package tests: 195 pass; typecheck clean.
- `bun run verify:cloud` (cloud lint + typecheck lanes, incl. the Worker bundle check): **passing** (83/83 tasks).

# Risks

**Low, with two deliberate behaviour changes.**

- Below the budgets nothing changes — proven byte-for-byte across a 38-case
  origin-vs-branch corpus covering both directions (status, refund decision,
  **and** the full body text).
- A caller request body over **1,000,000 bytes** now gets a typed `413` with the
  pre-charge refunded, where it previously succeeded at unbounded memory cost.
- An MCP response body over **5,000,000 bytes** now gets a typed `502` with the
  pre-charge refunded, where it previously succeeded, **was billed**, and was
  returned to the caller in full.
- Both ceilings are two constants derived from one number
  (`MAX_PROXY_REQUEST_BODY_BYTES` and a `x5` multiplier), copied from
  `services/oauth/credential-broker.ts`. If a maintainer wants different numbers
  for MCP specifically, that is a one-line change and I would rather be told than
  guess.
- Over-budget is never a truncated body served as success. The read is abandoned
  and the money is given back.

# Background

## What does this PR do?

`POST /api/mcp/proxy/:mcpId` buffers two bodies into the isolate with no byte
budget on either (`packages/cloud/api/mcp/proxy/[mcpId]/route.ts` on
`origin/develop`):

```
:126  export async function parseJsonBody(request: Request) {
:131    const text = await request.text();          <- caller's body, unbounded
...
:436  try {
:437    responseBody = await mcpResponse.text();    <- MCP's body, unbounded
```

The second one is the sharp end. `mcpResponse` comes from
`safeFetch(targetUrl, …)` where `targetUrl` is `mcp.external_endpoint` — a URL
the MCP's owner chose. `safeFetch` validates the target and pins the resolved
IP, which is the right SSRF guard; it has **no size cap and no deadline**. So
the number of bytes one proxied call spends inside the isolate is chosen by
whoever registered the MCP.

`:437` is not the last copy either: the string is handed to
`isJsonRpcErrorResponse()` (`:97`), which `JSON.parse`s the whole thing again
when it looks like an envelope, and then to `new Response(responseBody, …)`.

This package deploys as a Cloudflare Worker
(`packages/cloud/api/wrangler.toml`, `name = "eliza-cloud-api"`), where
per-isolate memory is a hard platform limit.

**On the existing protection, precisely.** Both reads *are* inside `try`/`catch`
and both catches are real — `refundPrecharge("mcp_response_read_failed")` then a
`502`. That handles a read *failure*: a reset socket, a decode error. It cannot
help here, because **there is no failure to catch — the read succeeds**. And
even if it threw, a `catch` runs after the allocation it would like to prevent.
The pre-charge/refund ledger around the call is correct and orthogonal: it
decides who pays, not how much memory is spent.

**Reachability.** `requireUserOrApiKeyWithOrg(c)` — any authenticated user with
an active organization. `resolveMcpProxyView` (`:115`) grants access to the
owner of an MCP *or* to any caller when the MCP `is_public`. A caller therefore
needs one MCP: a public one someone else registered, or one they registered
themselves pointed at a host they control — in which case the response size is
entirely their own choice.

## What kind of change is this?

Bug fix (non-breaking, except as stated under **Risks**).

## The fix

A new import-free module,
`packages/cloud/api/mcp/proxy/[mcpId]/proxy-body-budget.ts`, exporting
`readBodyTextWithinBudget(source, maxBytes, onCancelFailure?)`. It charges the
budget **before** the bytes are retained, in two stages:

1. a declared `content-length` over budget is refused **without reading the body
   at all**, and the body is cancelled best-effort;
2. otherwise the body is streamed and each chunk is charged against the running
   total **before** it is retained, so peak retention is the budget plus the
   chunk in hand. Decoding is incremental (`TextDecoder(…, { stream: true })`),
   so the raw bytes are not held alongside the finished string. A
   `content-length` that is absent, non-numeric, or not a safe integer is **not**
   treated as a budget grant.

The two ceilings are lifted from
`packages/cloud/shared/src/lib/services/oauth/credential-broker.ts` — the
platform's other "proxy one call to a caller-supplied host" service — and
derived the same way (#23900):

```ts
const MAX_PROXY_REQUEST_BODY_BYTES = 1_000_000;
const PROXY_RESPONSE_BODY_BUDGET_MULTIPLIER = 5;
const MAX_PROXY_RESPONSE_BODY_BYTES =
  MAX_PROXY_REQUEST_BODY_BYTES * PROXY_RESPONSE_BODY_BUDGET_MULTIPLIER;
```

so moving the request cap moves both. Over-budget refunds the pre-charge and
returns a typed `413` (request) or `502` (response), reusing the route's existing
`refundPrecharge(reason, metadata)` ledger with two new reasons,
`request_body_too_large` and `mcp_response_too_large`.

`parseJsonBody` keeps its exported signature and gains an optional `maxBytes`
that defaults to the request budget, so its existing unit tests in
`packages/cloud/api/__tests__/mcp-proxy-helpers.test.ts` continue to call it
exactly as before. The non-JSON `content-type` short-circuit still returns `{}`
without reading the body at all.

# Documentation changes needed?

My changes do not require a change to the project documentation.

# Testing

## Where should a reviewer start?

`packages/cloud/api/mcp/proxy/[mcpId]/route.ts` — two reads replaced, one typed

## Detailed testing steps

### 1. Allocation, origin vs branch, through the production seam

`safeFetch` returns a real WHATWG `Response`, so the production seam is
`Response.text()` on that object. The driver builds a real `Response` over a real
`ReadableStream` emitting 1 MiB chunks and samples `process.memoryUsage()` at
the instant the read resolves. Same 256 MiB upstream in every row:

| | declared `content-length` | RSS at read complete | `arrayBuffers` | heapUsed | outcome |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `origin/develop` | yes | **+776.5 MiB** | +256.0 MiB | +190.3 MiB | `200`, **billed**, 268,435,456-char body |
| `origin/develop` | no | **+777.2 MiB** | +256.0 MiB | +190.3 MiB | `200`, **billed** |
| `origin/develop`, real JSON envelope | no | **+776.6 MiB** | +256.0 MiB | +190.3 MiB | `200`, **billed** |
| this branch | yes | **+5.1 MiB** | +0.0 MiB | +0.0 MiB | `502`, refunded |
| this branch | no | **+14.0 MiB** | +0.0 MiB | +0.0 MiB | `502`, refunded |
| this branch, real JSON envelope | no | **+14.1 MiB** | +0.0 MiB | +0.0 MiB | `502`, refunded |

Note the outcome column on `develop`: this is not a request that fails
expensively — it **succeeds**, bills, and returns a quarter-gigabyte body.

### 2. No over-rejection — 38 cases, both directions, origin vs branch identical

Every case is traffic that succeeds on `develop` today. For each, two identical
real WHATWG objects are built and one is run through each sequence; status,
refund decision **and** the full body text are compared.

- Responses (each declared and chunked): empty, whitespace-only, a JSON-RPC
  `result`, a JSON-RPC `error` envelope (must still refund), an all-error batch,
  a partial-success batch (must still bill), non-JSON, malformed JSON, multi-byte
  UTF-8 repeated across chunk boundaries, a 900 KB result, a 4 MB result, and a
  body sized to the budget exactly.
- Requests (each declared and chunked): empty JSON body, a normal `tools/call`,
  multi-byte arguments, 900 KB of arguments, a non-JSON `content-type`, no
  `content-type` at all, and malformed JSON (must still throw `SyntaxError`).

```
corpus: 38 cases, identical=38, divergent=0
```

The multi-byte cases matter specifically: they prove the incremental
`TextDecoder` never splits a UTF-8 sequence across a chunk boundary.

### 3. Load-bearing revert, by copy-aside (not `git stash`)

The new module was copied aside and only the budget was neutralized inside it
(`maxBytes = Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY`), leaving the restructured read intact.
The 256 MiB response went straight back to `200` **billed** at +634.6 MiB RSS.
Restoring the file restored the `502` at +14.0 MiB.

### 4. Typecheck

The new module compiles clean under the package's own strict compiler settings,
TypeScript 6.0.3, zero diagnostics.

  on workerd; the *shape* — whole body materialized before any check on
  `develop`, not materialized on this branch — is a property of the code, not the
  runtime.
- **The hop is still un-deadlined.** Neither the `safeFetch` call nor the
  container-endpoint `fetch` carries an `AbortSignal`, so a slow MCP can hold the
  isolate for as long as the platform allows. That is a different mechanism (time,
  not bytes) with a different fix and it is deliberately not folded in here;
  #24050 records this PR's scope as the byte budgets.
- **No rate limit or per-key concurrency cap is added.** Nothing bounds how many
  proxied MCP calls one API key may make; this bounds the cost of each one.
- **Hosted CI checks do not run on this PR.** I contribute from a fork without
  push access to `elizaOS/eliza`, so no hosted check will report here, and
  nothing above should be read as "CI passed".

# What this PR does

- Replaces the established-phone repeat create/repair transaction with one indexed canonical delivery query shared by hosted Blooio/iMessage and Twilio Voice.
- Adds a dormant Durable Object Shared-account accelerator with canonical fallback.
- Adds a durable per-sender mutation fence around central user update/detach/delete writers. A fence is established before the canonical mutation, survives writer process death, forces canonical resolution, and is released only after the mutation completes.
- Prevents a concurrent fenced read from persisting stale `{userId, organizationId}` authority; overlapping writers keep independent tokens.
- Preserves a fresh-auth request outside the ordinary transport/status retry budget.
- Parses Blooio provider timestamps and emits provider-to-gateway latency.
- Emits Twilio target/history/token-directory stage timing in structured logs and `Server-Timing`.
- Preallocates Twilio's signed session/JTI and overlaps its required cross-worker revocation-directory write with independent returning-caller/history reads before TwiML. The exact preallocated identity is signed into the stream token; call scope, replay, expiry, revocation, and continuity gates remain intact.

The measured pre-change production baseline was `12.944s` warm and `21.351s` cold end to end. Model/Shared work was about `0.9–1.0s`; repeat account resolution was about `4.1s` on both paths.

# Risk and activation boundary

Medium, bounded to Personal Shared sender/account resolution and Twilio inbound setup. Projection miss, timeout, malformed output, or failure falls back to the existing canonical resolver.

The Durable Object accelerator is **not enabled in any checked-in environment**. Central lifecycle writers now prove the crash-safe protocol, but remaining direct identity/convergence/cutover writers must adopt the same fence before staging activation. Until then, the indexed canonical database resolver is the only enabled path.

No schema migration, UI, prompt, model, provider configuration, or secret-store change is included.

53:T195a,# Relates to

Closes #22575.

## What changed

- Registers `workflow_run_event` once per `AgentRuntime` in the canonical agent trigger worker, so standalone and app hosts use the same persisted trigger engine.
- Removes the duplicate app-core Smithers subscription while retaining its connector-event bridge.
- Lists trigger tasks with `agentIds: [runtime.agentId]`, re-reads each queued task before execution, and forwards the native Smithers event without runtime/function objects.
- Serializes events per saved trigger so concurrent emissions preserve current enabled/filter/run-count/max-run state.
- Derives a durable `WORKFLOW_DISPATCH` idempotency key from the saved trigger id plus Smithers native event id. Replays collapse; distinct triggers and distinct native events remain independent.
- Starts trigger processing without awaiting it from the Smithers emitter. Lookup and per-trigger failures go through `runtime.reportError`; one failed target neither rejects the source run nor blocks siblings.
- Extends the real local browser journey to create source/target Smithers workflows, save an exact-step trigger, run the source through the native service, and prove one target trigger execution plus `runCount === 1` after reload.

No second scheduler, HTTP loopback, Gateway protocol, or prose-based routing is introduced.

## Review correction

The predecessor head cached task snapshots for 500 ms and applied a one-second trigger throttle while awaiting the event handler. That could execute a just-disabled trigger, suppress distinct legitimate Smithers events, and delay the source run. Exact head replaces wall-clock admission with native event identity plus canonical dispatch idempotency and fresh serialized task state.

## Exact-head validation

Exact head: `8babb894f38c3d76f15d88d2c545cb6eb97f3cf5` (tree `5276592aee79aff83af942bb4ebafff61bbad15e`)

- Real local Chromium Smithers journey: 1/1 passed at exact head with recording, trace, screenshot, backend log, and persisted domain artifacts. It created source/target workflows, saved an exact-step trigger, observed one target execution in trigger mode with `runCount === 1`, ran manually, reloaded, and recovered source/widget state.
- Agent trigger runtime suite: 40/40 passed at exact head, including fresh discovery, concurrent state refresh, disable/delete rechecks, runtime isolation, replay idempotency, and distinct rapid events.
- App-core trigger bridge suite: 12/12 passed at exact head.
- plugin-workflow isolated suite: 16/16 files passed at exact head.
- plugin-workflow typecheck: passed.
- Exact-head changed-file Biome and `git diff --check`: passed.
- Agent/app-core/app package typechecks were attempted and remain blocked by missing optional/native workspace build artifacts outside this patch (Capacitor and optional plugin exports); no diagnostic names a changed implementation file.
- Exact-head validation receipt: https://github.com/elizaOS/eliza/releases/download/pr-evidence-9/22790-exact-head-validation.md

Activates the privacy-safe App Live Cloud evidence contracts from #23131 in the staging workflow:

- keeps production Cloud execution disabled by default for manual staging proof (run_cloud_production: false);
- drives the exact staging API origin through the locally built renderer and fails before Cloud traffic if that authority is inconsistent;
- proves one logical challenge turn across transport retries, then checks server-backed history after reload and a fresh BrowserContext;
- audits browser-visible create/provision/upgrade/delete routes and requires zero such mutations;
- records full-turn latency and continuity only through a closed, secret-free receipt;
- uploads no Playwright trace, screenshot, video, prompt, reply, token, or private identifier from the credentialed lane.

This PR is stacked on #23131. Retarget it to develop after #23131 merges.

## What

First codeable slice of the Linux GTK/WebKit shell work: the **signed artifact producer/verifier** implementing the cross-repo contract in `elizaOS/os:packages/os/linux/schemas/desktop-artifact-manifest.schema.json` (acceptance bullets "manifest entrypoints and archive digest verify" and "fixed adjacent manifest signature + manifest-named archive signature").

- `packages/app-core/scripts/package-linux-gtk-artifact.mjs` — `produce` / `verify` / `generate-key` CLI plus exported functions:
  - packages a staged shell build (`bin/eliza-desktop`, `bin/eliza-agent`, `bin/eliza-desktop-doctor` + payload) into `eliza-desktop-gtk-<version>-<arch>.tar.zst` for **x86_64, arm64, riscv64** from one code path;
  - refuses missing or non-executable entrypoints, bad arch/version/commit;
  - writes a schema-valid `desktop-artifact-manifest.json`, the fixed adjacent `desktop-artifact-manifest.json.sig` (Ed25519 over the exact manifest bytes) and `<archive-stem>.sig` (Ed25519 over the exact archive bytes);
  - verifier re-derives digest and both signatures from bytes, rejects linked contract files, audits archive member types/paths/link targets, and checks each entrypoint is a regular executable archive member.
- producer audits the staged tree, rejects unsafe links and special files, creates private build/key output exclusively, and publishes the complete set atomically with the manifest last.
- `packages/app-core/scripts/schemas/desktop-artifact-manifest.schema.json` — vendored byte-for-byte copy of the OS-repo contract, pinned by a drift test.
- `packages/app-core/scripts/__tests__/package-linux-gtk-artifact.test.ts` — 23 real-harness tests (real tar.zst via system tar, real Ed25519 keys): all three architectures round-trip, tampered-archive-byte rejection, tampered-manifest rejection, wrong-key rejection, entrypoint/stage refusals, full schema-violation matrix.
- `bun run --cwd packages/app-core build:linux-gtk-artifact` / `verify:linux-gtk-artifact` manifest scripts.

56:Tc10,Fixes #16921

## Summary

Implements the server/runtime-side owner-activation contract in `@elizaos/plugin-personal-assistant`:

- **`src/lifeops/first-run/activation.ts`** — `OwnerActivationService`: persists exactly ONE durable assistant activation turn per `owner+agent+contractVersion`. The turn's memory id is deterministic (`stringToUuid` of the activation key), so the durable write itself is the exactly-once anchor: retries, restarts, and a crash between the conversation write and the completion marker all reconcile to the same single turn (`already_complete`) instead of duplicating. Concurrent calls in one process share a single in-flight write.
- **Established-owner negative controls** — an owner with an existing `OwnerFactStore.primaryGoal`, real conversation history in the target room, or a prior contract-version activation is recorded `exempt` (with a typed reason) and receives no canned greeting, preserving #15149's silent entry. Bumping `OWNER_ACTIVATION_CONTRACT_VERSION` never re-activates silently; reactivation requires the explicit `reactivate: true` input.
- **Failure semantics** — a failed durable write throws `ElizaError` (`OWNER_ACTIVATION_WRITE_FAILED`, J2 wrap) and activation is NEVER marked complete; the HTTP boundary translates it to a retryable 503 (J1) so callers retry observably.
- **Routes** (`src/routes/first-run-activation-routes.ts`, wired through the existing OWNER/ADMIN gate in `routes/plugin.ts`): `POST /api/lifeops/first-run/activate` and `GET /api/lifeops/first-run/activation`. This is the server boundary the app onboarding flow calls when handing the owner to the live conversation — not a client check-then-write.
- **First LifeOps goal** — reuses the existing `ftu_goal_discovery` path rather than adding a goal store: the activation turn is goal-forward ("what's the one thing you most want my help with?"), and the evaluator persists the owner's answer into `OwnerFactStore.primaryGoal` exactly once.

## Verification

- `vitest run owner-activation` — **11/11 passed** (exactly-once + restart idempotency, crash reconciliation without a second turn, primary-goal and existing-history exemptions, failed-write-not-complete + successful retry, concurrent single write, explicit contract-version reactivation, route activate/status/400/503/retryable-503 translation).
- `bun run --cwd plugins/plugin-personal-assistant typecheck` — clean (after building `@elizaos/agent` dist).
- `biome check` on all touched files — clean.

57:Tc51,Fixes #19882

## What

Advances the two dispatcher-side residuals the merged bounded-authority slice (#22247) left open on the tracker: **per-domain policy hooks** and **submit interception**.

- **`plugins/plugin-browser/src/browser-domain-policy.ts` (new)** — pluggable `BrowserDomainPolicy` registry on a `globalThis` symbol (same pattern as `browser-capture-hooks.ts`) so both the `BrowserService` dispatcher and the module-level workspace form path consult one source of truth. Evaluation is fail-closed: a throwing policy blocks, an unrecognized verdict blocks, the first non-allow decision wins, and with no registered policies behavior is unchanged. Includes a subaction side-effect classifier (unknown subactions classify as mutating, never read) and a built-in `createBrowserDomainAllowlistPolicy` with `block` / `require_confirmation` verdicts that fails closed on unresolvable domains and rejects suffix-spoofed hosts (`notexample.com` does not match `example.com`).
- **`browser-service.ts`** — `execute()` evaluates every command, including nested batch steps, against registered policies before target selection; non-allow decisions surface as typed `POLICY_BLOCKED` `BrowserDispatchFailure`s (with a distinct message for `require_confirmation`). Nothing has executed at that point, so blocking is side-effect free. The pre-existing generic eval/upload hard block is untouched and independent of policy registration.
- **`workspace/browser-workspace-forms.ts`** — submit interception at the only point where the resolved form-submit URL is known (`submitWebBrowserWorkspaceForm`), before any bytes leave: a click that turns into a cross-domain form submit re-evaluates policies with effect `submit` against the actual submit-URL domain and fails closed.
- Barrel export + bundle-safety binding in `index.ts`; plugin `CLAUDE.md`/`AGENTS.md` updated (byte-identical, parity gate green).

## Tests

20 new deterministic tests in `src/__tests__/browser-domain-policy.test.ts` exercising the real registry, the real `BrowserService` dispatcher, and the real JSDOM workspace submit path (no mock of the system under test). Adversarial coverage: throwing policies, malformed verdicts, empty/whitespace allowlists, suffix-spoofed domains, non-http(s) URLs, unknown-domain fail-closed submits, nested-batch smuggling, and eval hard-block bypass via an allow-everything policy.

- `bun run --cwd plugins/plugin-browser test` — 31 files / 259 tests pass
- `bun run --cwd plugins/plugin-browser typecheck` — pass

Fixes #23834

Definition of Done: full standard in [`CONTRIBUTING.md`](../CONTRIBUTING.md).

## What changed

- Implements TikTok's sequential decimal-byte ranged upload protocol with tail merging and exact `206` intermediate / `201` final validation.
- Restricts provider-returned upload URLs to documented HTTPS TikTok upload hosts, then sends them through the shared DNS/private-network guard with redirects rejected.
- Validates and preserves MP4, QuickTime, and WebM MIME types.
- Cancels every ranged-upload response body on success and failure.
- Retries identical ranges after authoritative 5xx responses and reconciles ambiguous transport/final-response loss before replay.
- Treats a `416` replay as committed only when TikTok's progress receipt proves the exact range was received.
- Returns an explicit credit hold for unresolved remote outcomes so a possibly published post is neither duplicated nor refunded as a known failure.
- Uses a 10 MiB base64 admission budget with strict raw MIME-wrapping overhead and a 32 MiB binary ceiling so overlapping Worker uploads remain below the isolate memory limit. Larger media remains URL-backed and the broader #23834 work adds streamed object storage.

# What changed

This five-file corrective patch closes the source-level safety defects found after #23360:

1. Terraform backup values enter the root-sourced environment only as base64 and are decoded after parsing, so valid secret characters cannot become shell syntax.
2. Destructive restore authority comes from a one-use server-side `eliza.restore_target_id=drill-<uuid>` identity, not a bypassable hostname blocklist.
3. Globals restore is fail-fast with `ON_ERROR_STOP=1`.
4. Every restored tenant role must authenticate to its own database through direct Postgres and the isolated pgbouncer; cross-database probes must fail with an explicit Postgres CONNECT denial.
5. Backup-retention enumeration now fails closed instead of swallowing `rclone lsf` failures, and all retained untrusted parsing catches carry the repository error-policy classification.
6. The target must have no role collision with `globals.sql`, so strict globals replay cannot die on or overwrite a bootstrap role. The runbook requires a unique disposable bootstrap superuser.
7. Every psql call ignores startup files. The nonce guard raises a real SQL error in the same session before globals, database drops/creates, and each database's rendered pg_restore SQL. Rendering without `--create` eliminates unguarded reconnects and line-rewrite corruption.

The probe manifest contains opaque dump ids, roles, and password environment-variable names only. Passwords travel through `PGPASSWORD`; they are not placed in command arguments or reports. The operator runbook documents disposable-target provisioning, protected probe metadata, verification, and teardown.

# Risks

Medium. This raises the first-party document-store capability to v3 and makes
custom adapters fail closed until they implement atomic revision replacement.
Replacement fragment IDs must also be fresh: reusing a committed fragment ID
is rejected before any secondary-index or SQL mutation, which preserves the old
generation across rollback and asynchronous PGlite write-back.

# Background

## What does this PR do?

- stages and validates every replacement fragment and embedding before storage
  publication;
- atomically row-locks the SQL parent, verifies the expected revision/scope,
  replaces the complete fragment generation, and updates the parent in one real
  Drizzle transaction;
- gives in-memory adapters serialized copy/swap semantics and gates vector
  readers on the same document mutation barrier;
- rejects IDs from the committed fragment generation before staging, preventing
  failed in-memory edits from deleting the old vector and preventing a
  zero-fragment PGlite write-back window;
- publishes PGlite/Electric write-back notifications only after the winning
  local transaction commits, using the exact removed fragment IDs;
- preserves the complete old revision on embedding, insert, delete, collision,
  or competing-writer failure; and
- accepts WhatsApp idempotency adapters with the canonical v2+ method surface
  instead of rejecting every new v3 adapter by exact version equality.

The already-landed create-path ingestion state machine is unchanged. This PR
corrects and completes the consolidated `updateDocument` residual from #16021.

## What kind of change is this?

Bug fix (non-breaking for first-party adapters; intentionally fail-closed for
incomplete custom document adapters and reused replacement fragment IDs).

# Risks

Low. Scope is confined to `PushTokenRegistry` and its two HTTP routes. Behavior changes are strictly hardening: the durable cache format is unchanged (`{ token, platform, createdAt }[]`), and hydration now normalizes legacy/dirty rows into that same shape. The only externally-visible surface change is the exported constant rename `MAX_PUSH_TOKEN_LENGTH` → `MAX_PUSH_TOKEN_BYTES` (both were internal to the agent package; only these files imported it). New validation can now reject previously-accepted malformed rows (that is the intent) and returns HTTP 400 instead of silently upserting.

# Background

## What does this PR do?

PR #23015 added a 64-record in-memory cap, but the merged implementation crossed resource and consistency boundaries *before* that cap took effect. This PR closes those gaps:

1. **Bound hydration before work.** `MAX_PERSISTED_PUSH_TOKENS` (16× the live cap = 1024) is the largest stored array the registry will traverse. A cache row longer than that is rejected fail-closed to empty **without** filter/copy/sort — worst-case hydration is a single `Array.isArray`/`length` check. Fail-closed does **not** destroy the durable row (a later mutation overwrites it), so a transient never nukes a large legitimate dump.
2. **Validate at the persistence boundary.** One pure validator (`parsePushTokenRecord` / `assertValidToken`) enforces: trimmed non-empty token, token within an explicit **UTF-8 byte** cap (`MAX_PUSH_TOKEN_BYTES = 4096`, computed with `Buffer.byteLength(token, "utf8")`, not char length), supported platform (`ios`|`android`), and a finite, non-negative, safe-integer timestamp. The same checks gate hydrate and `register`/`unregister`.
3. **Dedup-before-cap.** Keep the newest valid record per token, **then** apply the 64 live cap. Duplicate-heavy data can no longer underfill the registry (see domain repro below).
4. **Durable repair.** When a bounded-but-dirty legacy dump is normalized, the repaired form is persisted **once** (guarded by a canonical-form check so a clean load never rewrites). Best-effort: a failed repair write only re-normalizes on the next start and is reported via `runtime.reportError`, never failing the read path.
5. **Transactional mutations.** `register`/`unregister` snapshot the `Map`, mutate, then `commit()`. On a rejected `setCache` the snapshot is restored (observable registry unchanged) and a typed `ElizaError` (`PUSH_TOKEN_PERSIST_FAILED`) is thrown. The same-process mutation queue keeps processing later ops after a failure (no wedge).
6. **Uniform byte bound + HTTP mapping.** The byte cap now applies to direct callers **and both DELETE route shapes** (`{ token }` body and legacy `/:token`). Typed validation failures (`PUSH_TOKEN_INVALID`) map to **400** via `isPushTokenValidationError`; genuine persistence failures propagate to the server's **500** boundary and are never swallowed into a fake success.
7. **ElizaError + redaction.** New domain failures use `ElizaError` codes + context. Tokens never appear in any error message or log (only byte length / counts).

**Concurrency scope (per acceptance criterion 8):** cross-process compare-and-swap is out of scope — the runtime cache contract exposes no transactional CAS primitive. Atomicity here is guaranteed **within a single process** only. This is stated in the class header and in `commit()`.

## What kind of change is this?

Bug fix / hardening (non-breaking except the internal `MAX_PUSH_TOKEN_LENGTH` → `MAX_PUSH_TOKEN_BYTES` constant rename).

# Documentation changes needed?

My changes do not require project-docs changes. The behavior contract is documented in the class header of `push-token-registry.ts` and in the two test-file headers.

5f:T1061,Fixes #19886

## What

Adds the Cloud credential broker used by first-party plugins for OAuth token refresh and provider API calls. Plugins reference credentials only by opaque connection ID; the broker resolves, refreshes, and injects the provider credential entirely server-side.

- `packages/cloud/shared/src/lib/services/oauth/credential-broker.ts` — the broker service (`CredentialBroker`, DI-friendly `createCredentialBroker`, production `credentialBroker` wired to `oauthService`), with per-platform audience pins (`BROKER_PLATFORM_POLICIES`: exact provider API hostnames for google/microsoft/linear/notion/github/slack/hubspot/asana/dropbox/airtable/zoom/jira/linkedin/twitter).
- `POST /api/v1/connections/:id/broker` — execute one provider request through the connection's credential.
- `POST /api/v1/connections/:id/refresh` — refresh/revalidate the token; returns metadata only (`refreshed`, `expiresAt`, `scopes`) — never token material.
- Router regenerated (`bun run codegen`, 679 routes mounted).

## Security invariants

- **Opaque IDs only**: raw tokens never appear in responses, errors, or logs (asserted in tests).
- **Strip inbound Eliza auth**: the upstream request is built from scratch from the validated JSON body; inbound Authorization/cookies are never forwarded. Caller-supplied credential-bearing headers (`authorization`, `cookie`, `x-api-key`, `x-eliza-*`, `host`, `x-forwarded-*`, …) are rejected with 400, not silently stripped; remaining headers must pass a generic + per-platform allowlist; CR/LF injection rejected.
- **Audience pinning**: https only, exact-hostname allowlist per platform, no userinfo, no ports; lookalike/subdomain hosts rejected. Platforms without a pin (e.g. twilio/blooio) cannot be brokered.
- **No redirect following**: `redirect: "manual"` so a credentialed request never chases an upstream Location.
- **Org/user binding**: connection must resolve under the caller's organization; a user-owned connection is invisible (404) to other users; org-shared connections remain usable; revoked → 401 reconnect-required; expired/pending/error → 401.
- **Refresh race/idempotency**: refresh goes through `oauthService.getValidToken` (versioned token cache + adapter refresh); repeated refreshes are idempotent and report `refreshed: false` when the cached token is still valid.
- Upstream response headers relayed through an allowlist (no `set-cookie`); binary payloads returned base64; 30s upstream deadline; transport failure becomes a typed error with no header/token egress.

## Tests

`packages/cloud/shared/src/lib/services/oauth/credential-broker.test.ts` — 34 deterministic tests with protocol-faithful fetch stub and injected connection/token lookups (no mock of the system under test): hostile URL/host/header/redirect cases, org/user binding, revoked/expired auth, token-egress redaction on success and failure paths, provider 401 passthrough, oversized body, binary payloads, refresh idempotency.

# Risks

**Low, with one deliberate behaviour change that this PR measures rather than
asserts.**

- Below the budget nothing changes — proven byte-for-byte across a 29-case
  origin-vs-branch corpus (status **and** exact response body).
- The budget bounds the whole multipart **envelope**, not the file. It is
  `MAX_BYTES + MULTIPART_ENVELOPE_HEADROOM_BYTES` = 5 MiB + 1 MiB = 6,291,456
  bytes. A request whose file is within the 5 MiB cap but whose *envelope*
  exceeds 6 MiB — e.g. a 5 MiB avatar plus 2 MiB of additional form fields —
  now gets a `413` where it previously succeeded. The same driver that proves
  the corpus also prints this case explicitly, with the byte counts, so the
  change is visible rather than inferred. Neither route reads any field except
  `file`, so 1 MiB of headroom is far more than the framing actually needs; if a
  maintainer wants a different number it is one constant.
- The read now consumes `c.req.raw.body` and re-wraps it, instead of Hono's
  cached `c.req.formData()`. Nothing downstream in either handler reads the body
  again.

# Background

## What does this PR do?

Both avatar upload routes declare a 5 MiB cap and then consult it one statement
after the whole multipart body has already been parsed into memory. Identical
code in both files on `origin/develop`:

```
:22   const MAX_BYTES = 5 * 1024 * 1024;
...
:53   const form = await c.req.formData();      <- parses AND materializes every part
:58   if (entry.size > MAX_BYTES) { ... 400 }    <- asks after paying
```

`formData()` does not hand back a lazy handle: it parses the envelope and
materializes each part, so `entry.size` cannot be consulted until the bytes the
comparison exists to refuse are already resident. This package deploys as a
Cloudflare Worker (`packages/cloud/api/wrangler.toml`,
`name = "eliza-cloud-api"`), where per-isolate memory is a hard platform limit.

**On the existing protection, precisely.** Both handlers *are* wrapped —
`try { … } catch (error) { return failureResponse(c, error); }` — and that
catch is real: it maps auth, quota and object-storage failures to the canonical
API error, and the R2/quota compensation logic around it is careful. It cannot
help here, because a `catch` runs *after* the allocation it would like to
prevent. The 400 arrives on top of the spend, not instead of it. Both routes are
also behind `rateLimit(RateLimitPresets.STANDARD)`, which bounds how *many*
requests an org may make, not what one of them costs — and one is enough.

**Reachability.** `requireUserOrApiKeyWithOrg(c)` — any authenticated user with
an active organization. The routes accept `multipart/form-data` and the body
size is whatever the client sends.

## What kind of change is this?

Bug fix (non-breaking, except as stated under **Risks**).

## The fix

A new import-free module,
`packages/cloud/api/_lib/multipart-body-budget.ts`, exporting
`readRequestWithinMultipartBudget(request, maxBytes, onCancelFailure?)`. It
charges the budget **before** the body is parsed, in two stages:

1. a declared `content-length` over budget is refused **without reading the body
   at all**, and the upload is cancelled best-effort;
2. otherwise the body is streamed and each chunk is charged against the running
   total **before** it is retained, so peak retention is the budget plus the
   chunk in hand. A `content-length` that is absent, non-numeric, or not a safe
   integer is **not** treated as a budget grant.

On success it hands back a `Request` with the same URL, method and headers
(minus `content-length`, which no longer describes the buffered body) so the
handler goes on to `.formData()` exactly as before.

Both stages are copied from `packages/cloud/api/v1/voice/stt/route.ts:370`
(`readRequestWithMultipartLimit`), the other multipart upload in this package,
which already does exactly this for its own limit. It is module-private there
and welded to the STT byte constants and 413 body, so the shape is reused rather
than the function; the new module is placed in `api/_lib` (alongside the
existing `api/compat/_lib` convention) because these two routes live in
different trees and would otherwise duplicate it.

The budget itself is derived, not a third literal:

```ts
const MAX_BYTES = 5 * 1024 * 1024;
const MULTIPART_ENVELOPE_HEADROOM_BYTES = 1024 * 1024;
const MAX_MULTIPART_BODY_BYTES = MAX_BYTES + MULTIPART_ENVELOPE_HEADROOM_BYTES;
```

so moving the file cap moves the envelope budget with it.

## Why both routes in one PR

`my-agents/characters/avatar/route.ts` and `v1/user/avatar/route.ts` are the
same handler twice: same `MAX_BYTES`, same `ALLOWED` set, same `isFile` helper,
same read, same check, same 400 body. They are already tested together by one
file (`packages/cloud/api/__tests__/avatar-storage-quota.test.ts`, which imports
both route modules and runs one table of cases against each). Fixing one and not
the other would leave the identical defect on the identical line.

# Documentation changes needed?

My changes do not require a change to the project documentation.

## Detailed testing steps

### 1. Allocation, origin vs branch, through the production seam

Hono's `c.req.formData()` is a cached passthrough to `c.req.raw.formData()`, so
the production seam is `Request.formData()` on the real request. The driver
builds a real WHATWG `Request` whose body is a real `ReadableStream` carrying a
real multipart envelope (`--boundary`, `Content-Disposition`, `Content-Type`,
1 MiB payload chunks, closing delimiter) and samples `process.memoryUsage()` at
the instant the parse resolves — before the `entry.size > MAX_BYTES` line runs.

| | upload | declared `content-length` | RSS at parse complete | status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `origin/develop` | 4 MiB (a normal avatar) | yes | +15.2 MiB | `200` |
| `origin/develop` | 256 MiB | yes | **+776.5 MiB** | `400` "File too large (max 5MB)" |
| `origin/develop` | 256 MiB | no | **+776.5 MiB** | `400` "File too large (max 5MB)" |
| this branch | 4 MiB (a normal avatar) | yes | +20.3 MiB | `200` |
| this branch | 256 MiB | yes | **+3.9 MiB** | `413` |
| this branch | 256 MiB | no | **+10.8 MiB** | `413` |

`develop` enforces a 5 MiB cap at a cost of three quarters of a gigabyte. On this
branch the declared case never reads the body, and the chunked case stops at the
budget plus the chunk in hand.

### 2. No over-rejection — 29 cases, origin vs branch, identical

Every case is an upload that succeeds (or fails identically) on `develop` today.
Two identical `Request`s per case; status **and** exact JSON body compared.

- File sizes 1 B, 1 KiB, 1 MiB, 4 MiB, `MAX_BYTES - 1`, and `MAX_BYTES` exactly,
  each declared and chunked.
- A jpeg at the cap, a gif with a 512 KiB additional `notes` form field, an
  over-cap file that already 400s on `develop`, an unsupported MIME, a wrong
  field name, and a body with no parts at all.
- Five untrustworthy `content-length` headers on a valid 1 KiB upload:
  `"abc"`, `"0x400"`, `"-1"`, `"99999999999999999999"`, `""`.

```
corpus: 29 cases, identical=29, divergent=0
```

The same driver then prints the one intended divergence with its byte counts —
see **Risks**.

### 3. Load-bearing revert, by copy-aside (not `git stash`)

The new module was copied aside and only the budget was neutralized inside it
(`maxBytes = Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY`), leaving the restructured read intact.
The 256 MiB upload went back to `400` "File too large (max 5MB)" at **+1034.8
MiB RSS** (higher than `develop` because the re-wrap adds a copy when the budget
is not enforcing anything). Restoring the file restored `413` at +10.8 MiB.

### 4. Typecheck

The new module compiles clean under the package's own strict compiler settings,
TypeScript 6.0.3, zero diagnostics.

## Known gaps / failures

- **`bun run verify` was not run, and neither was the `packages/cloud` package
  typecheck nor `packages/cloud/api/__tests__/avatar-storage-quota.test.ts`** —
  the existing suite that drives both of these route modules. This machine could
  not complete a workspace install: the checkout lives on an external volume
  measured at ~1.6 MB/s under concurrent load, and `bun install` did not finish.
  Everything above was produced without `node_modules` by driving the real new
  module — deliberately import-free for exactly this reason — under `bun`. That
  suite builds its uploads with `FormData` + `route.request(...)`, which
  produces small in-budget bodies, so it should be unaffected; that is reasoning,
  not a green run, and closing it is the gap a reviewer should close.
- **`biome` was not run** on the touched files, for the same reason.
- **No new test file is added**: a `__tests__` entry that has never been executed
  would be a claim, not evidence. The natural home is
  `avatar-storage-quota.test.ts`, which already runs one table of cases against
  both route modules; I will add oversize cases there in this PR if a maintainer
  prefers that to merging the fix first.
- **Node/bun `formData()` is not workerd.** The absolute MiB figures would differ
  on workerd; the *shape* — whole body materialized before the check on
  `develop`, not materialized on this branch — is a property of the code, not the
  runtime. Bun's parser also derives `File.type` from the filename extension
  rather than the part's `Content-Type`, which is why the corpus names each file
  to match the MIME it exercises; both arms see byte-identical input either way.
- **Three sibling routes have the same shape and are deliberately not touched.**
  `v1/files/route.ts` (`MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES` 50 MiB × `MAX_UPLOAD_FILES` 10, both
  checked after the parse — its own permitted maximum is already 500 MiB),
  `v1/voice/clone/route.ts` (`MAX_TOTAL_SIZE` 100 MiB), and
  `v1/documents/pre-upload/route.ts`. Their declared ceilings are per-file or
  per-batch totals that already exceed what an isolate can hold, so charging a
  whole-envelope budget there is a decision about what the real ceiling should
  be, not a mechanical port of this diff. They are named in the issue as
  deserving their own.
- **Hosted CI checks do not run on this PR.** I contribute from a fork without
  push access to `elizaOS/eliza`, so no hosted check will report here, and
  nothing above should be read as "CI passed".

# What does this PR do?

Bounds remote-runner HTTP response bodies, validates response schemas, keeps request deadlines active through body consumption, makes rejected-body teardown nonblocking, preserves per-call deadline snapshots and stable timeout/abort identity, and carries the remote runner structured `timedOut` result through the public terminal contract.

# Testing

Exact head: `fd3f1b6a7a193ecb67588b6782f6ddd0cbeba16e`. The complete focused suite passed 49/51 before the final current-base contract reconciliation exposed two semantic mismatches. After correcting both, exact targeted tests for timer-range validation and structured timeout propagation pass 2/2. The subsequent latest-`develop` rebase was conflict-free. Both files pass Biome and diff checks.

## Current-source audit and implementation plan — 2026-09-06

Baseline: `8fea4f94c29c7712ce3caf303e3350150622d048`. This is the canonical all-view campaign, with a six-person-day Sprint 2 execution tranche and a separate Sprint 3 continuation. No live UI/device/provider acceptance was run in this audit.

### Reconciled landed work and current source

- [#24198](https://github.com/elizaOS/eliza/pull/24198) merged on August 22: Browser/Finance/readiness first tranche. [#24400](https://github.com/elizaOS/eliza/pull/24400) also merged that day: Phone/Messages duplicate controls, Calendar cleanup and inert LifeOps registration. Historical draft status and failing capture counts in comments are not current blockers or current proof.
- Current PhoneView and MessagesView are single data wrappers returning one spatial presentation. Do not remove their spatial children as duplicates: those are the rendered presentation owners. Native calls still originate in the wrappers; the all-channel operation/authorization proof must follow those native boundaries rather than infer parity from one visible button.
- Calendar evolved after the old cleanup: [the public CalendarView export now aliases CalendarPage](https://github.com/elizaOS/eliza/blob/8fea4f94c29c7712ce3caf303e3350150622d048/plugins/plugin-calendar/src/index.ts#L54-L67), which mounts CalendarSection. SimpleCalendarView remains an explicitly documented compact projection export. Do not reinstate the older “CalendarView aliases SimpleCalendarView” architecture or remove that projection without current consumer/package compatibility analysis.
- #30222 and #30231 remain open, but current source already mounts CalendarSection and supplies explicit seven-column inline grid styles in [MonthGrid](https://github.com/elizaOS/eliza/blob/8fea4f94c29c7712ce3caf303e3350150622d048/plugins/plugin-calendar/src/components/CalendarSection.tsx#L780-L800). Their original source defects are not automatically current defects. Verify the served bundle/source and desktop/mobile behavior with those owners before scheduling duplicate repairs.
- The old Cloud primitives/navigation complaint is stale: [CloudView imports canonical Card/Badge/Button plus guarded navigation/external opening](https://github.com/elizaOS/eliza/blob/8fea4f94c29c7712ce3caf303e3350150622d048/plugins/plugin-elizacloud/src/components/cloud/CloudView.tsx#L18-L76). It has real loading/signed-out/error/ready state modeling and a state-machine test suite. Retain those and inspect actual interaction/backing result rather than rewrite already-fixed primitives.
- State-story breadth remains incomplete in the inspected packages: no stories reference the shipped PhoneSpatialView, MessagesSpatialView, CalendarPage or CloudView; the cloud package has an ElizaCloudDashboard story, which is a different component. Confirm current Storybook discovery/aliases before adding focused state stories to the canonical rendered components. Existing component tests do not provide all visual states automatically.

### Why existing green audits would not complete this issue

1. [The generic all-view interaction smoke test](https://github.com/elizaOS/eliza/blob/8fea4f94c29c7712ce3caf303e3350150622d048/packages/app/test/ui-smoke/all-views-interaction.spec.ts#L13-L39) uses a renderer fixture, a route list and explicit maxima of 24 clicks/8 inputs per view. This is useful smoke coverage, not proof of every operation, nested state, gesture, keyboard path or real provider mutation.
2. [The visual case builder](https://github.com/elizaOS/eliza/blob/8fea4f94c29c7712ce3caf303e3350150622d048/packages/app/test/ui-smoke/aesthetic-audit-view-cases.ts#L1-L75) still contains a hand-maintained built-in route mapping and consumes a plugin case registry. The aesthetic capture also intercepts cloud/views API calls. Good fixture screenshots cannot be relabeled real account/device evidence or a complete target inventory.
3. #23110 has a merged declaration generator, but the exhaustive semantic ledger draft #24343 closed unmerged; #28958 is open and cross-registry reconciliation remains relevant. Do not revive the rejected static heuristic ledger or treat old per-operation counts as the campaign denominator.
4. Phone's status read currently degrades to null and `canPlaceCalls` defaults true if missing. Test the real native status-failure boundary before claiming correct unavailable/disabled behavior; this is a source-backed optimistic fallback, not an observed real-device incident. Messages has separate SMS-role and send-in-flight state that needs real supported-target proof. Browser-only mocks cannot certify either.

### Ordered execution and implementation plan

1. **Build the current denominator.** Consume #23110's target/runtime/operation reconciliation and #28958's canonical route owners. Record every production view, target, operation and owning service/action, plus internal/preview/unsupported exclusions with reasons. Join actual enabled controls to operations, including nested dialogs, menus, keyboard, drag/drop and gestures. Missing classification is an unresolved row, never a pass or arbitrary view-only exemption.
2. **Baseline served artifacts before testing.** Record source SHA, build/install identity, API/runtime identity and loaded plugin bundle hashes. Verify the currently installed/served Calendar fixes rather than infer them from GitHub or a stale process. Capture baseline desktop/mobile and relevant device views before editing; use actual role/account states where the operation needs them.
3. **Calibrate critical operations first.** Execute Calendar create/edit/draft and denied/failing source, Notes create/update and persistence, Todos complete/reopen, Settings save/reload and rejection. Drive both direct UI and chat/voice against the same backing record and compare typed outcomes/receipt IDs. Determine actual test/remediation cost; six days is an execution budget, not an all-repairs guarantee.
4. **Expand by view family with deterministic isolation.** Exercise every remaining production operation under a named owner. Each result row includes actor/role, target, prerequisites, action/arguments, expected state transition, actual backing receipt, UI/agent outcome, and pass/fail/blocked. Reset only explicitly owned test data; distinguish side-effect preview from applied change. Read and mutation evidence per view is a starting sample, not a substitute for the complete ledger.
5. **Repair reproduced failures at the owning layer.** Examples to investigate include Phone status failure enabling a call control, Messages duplicate send/role loss, Calendar mode/source/bundle problems and Cloud unavailable/retry/link-out behavior. Extract shared business use-cases only where an actual view/action divergence is demonstrated. Preserve compatibility exports and existing domain owners; add a bounded issue only for a reproduced caller-visible failure needing separate ownership.

## Independent adversarial review #24104 — 2026-09-06

Baseline `b676280384b15df54204276e34bb8740db26936f`. Reviewed the full generic interaction oracle, request/response observers, special workflow observer and route-denominator source; no browser/device/provider action occurred.

## P1 — Generic smoke green can mean an unrelated request or rejected operation, even below its coverage caps

The prior audit correctly rejected “all controls” from capped counts but missed the stronger oracle flaw. `semanticDelta` (packages/app/test/ui-smoke/all-views-interaction.spec.ts:380–424) accepts any increase in page-wide API request count before examining the control. `observeClickOutcome` at 491–521 immediately returns observed for that delta. Request collection at 817 observes all /api/ requests; response failures at 822 only record >=500. A background polling request, or the clicked operation's 4xx, can satisfy “semantic outcome” without a persisted effect.

Executed a dependency-free probe of the actual source function: extracted only semanticDelta, transpiled with pinned Bun 1.3.14's built-in TypeScript transpiler, and invoked with identical URL/DOM/control snapshot plus apiRequestCount 0→1. Returned `API request count changed 0 -> 1`. Identical snapshot with count unchanged returned null. This proves the oracle's acceptance rule, not an executed product bug. No modified copy was written into the repository.

Disconfirming evidence: the suite already recognizes this for workflows (comment and workflowSurfaceResponses at 834 onward) and separately asserts that workflow surface's successful sequence. Do not claim every workflow failure is hidden. The generic cross-view oracle still lacks that operation-specific observation.

Amendment: before expanding the campaign, classify this suite as interaction/transport activity smoke only. Drive each acceptance operation through its specific correlated request/response and owning persisted-state observer. For an expected denied/error case, assert the intended error plus no mutation; for a success case, require committed effect/receipt, never arbitrary DOM error text or traffic. Add an oracle negative control with background polling and a rejected mutation returning 4xx. Avoid solving it by banning all 4xx globally because denied-state scenarios legitimately require them.

## P2 — UI enumeration can omit entire navigation classes; denominator must come from operation authority

CLICK_SELECTOR at line 41 enumerates buttons/roles and only anchors whose href begins '#'; INPUT_SELECTOR excludes file inputs. Thus normal href links, upload/drop targets, gestures and controls appearing only after state changes are outside generic enumeration, independent of 24/8 maxima. The hand-maintained VIEW_ROUTES file is explicitly built-in smoke/aesthetic scope, not all plugin view operations. The previous proposal to join runtime controls with #23110 remains necessary, but increasing caps cannot produce completeness.

Amendment: acceptance ledger includes operation modality (anchor/navigation, file picker/drop, keyboard/gesture, nested dialog) and actual target fixture. Distinguish a genuine no-op from an unenumerated control. Do not run a generic click-everything loop against a real billing/device/account fixture; use isolated operation-specific cases with authorized effects and reversible cleanup.

## Dependency/capacity correction

#23110 need not finish its broad semantic ledger before any QA begins: freeze a measured critical-operation denominator, execute it, then append unresolved families to the same campaign. But do not close #24104 or treat the six-day tranche as all-view coverage. Existing five-cycle visual requirement checks pixels/states and cannot substitute for the corrected effect oracle.

6e:T8d9,## Summary

`selectReplayEvents` in `packages/agent/src/api/ws-event-replay.ts` is documented to cap replays "to the `limit` most recent so a stale cursor can never replay an unbounded burst", but any `limit <= 0` (or `NaN`) **inverts the cap into a full-buffer replay**. The clamp maps invalid limits to `cap = 0`, and `Array.slice(-0)` behaves as `slice(0)` — a full copy — so the "replay nothing" case replays everything.

## Affected code path

- `packages/agent/src/api/ws-event-replay.ts:94-102`

```ts
const cap = limit > 0 ? limit : 0;
if (cursor === null) {
  return cap >= buffer.length ? buffer.slice() : buffer.slice(-cap); // slice(-0) === slice(0)
}
...
return missing.length > cap ? missing.slice(-cap) : missing;        // same inversion
```

Both the no-cursor path and the cursor path fail open. The buffer holds up to `maxBufferedEvents` (1500) envelopes, so an inverted cap floods the client with the entire buffer instead of nothing.

## Reproduction (verified on current `develop`, commit aeae937584)

```ts
selectReplayEvents([{eventId:"evt-1"},{eventId:"evt-2"},{eventId:"evt-3"}], null, 0);
// → all three events   (expected: [])
selectReplayEvents(buffer, null, -5);
// → full buffer       (expected: [])
selectReplayEvents(buffer, 1, NaN);
// → every event past seq 1   (expected: [])
```

## Reachability

The sole production caller (`api/server.ts` WS replay) passes the constant `DEFAULT_REPLAY_LIMIT = 120`, so the inversion is not reachable over HTTP today. But `selectReplayEvents` is an exported bounding primitive with its own unit-test file, and its JSDoc states the safety contract; any future caller that wires `limit` to a query parameter or config inherits a fail-open flood instead of a bounded replay. The existing test suite never covers `limit <= 0`.

## Expected behavior

A non-positive or non-numeric limit means "replay nothing" — the safe direction for a cap whose purpose is burst prevention.

## Proposed fix direction

Return `[]` when the clamped cap is zero:

```ts
const cap = limit > 0 ? limit : 0;
if (cap === 0) return [];
```

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `limit = 0`, negative, and `NaN` return `[]` on both the no-cursor and cursor paths.
- [ ] Existing replay tests keep passing unchanged.

## Change

**Lift, not copy**: `packages/agent/src/api/realpath-confinement.ts` moves to `@elizaos/shared/platform/path-confinement` verbatim (null-returning fail-closed walk, errno-narrowed, J3-tagged); the three agent call sites import the shared subpath directly, no re-export shim. Deep-import only — deliberately NOT added to shared's root barrel, which browser/UI code consumes and which must not pull `node:fs`.

**plugin-coding-tools consumes it**, replacing the last fail-open walk (bare catch swallowing every errno, climbing past dangling/EACCES ancestors, lexical fallback return) and the pre-#22408 `..`-prefix `isWithin` bug (`..safe.js` false-denied inside an allowed root).

**sandbox-service policy is decided per direction, not inherited.** Entries keep BOTH spellings `{lexical, canonical|null}` and are never dropped on resolution failure — a blocklist that shrinks on error fails open, and dropping the last allow-root would silently disable the allowlist (`validatePath` skips it when the list is empty). The two matchers are deliberately asymmetric:

- **blocklist**: any-spelling × any-spelling (over-blocking is the safe direction) — pinned by an aliasing test and a post-start symlink-retarget drift test;
- **allowlist**: the CANONICAL candidate only. A symmetric matcher was tried first and the existing workspace-escape test caught it live: lexical admission re-admits a symlink whose real target escaped the root. The `?? lexical` root fallback covers an EACCES-at-init root that resolves later (pinned by a chmod test, skipped as uid 0);
- an unresolvable candidate refuses outright (`unresolvable_path`; all 8 `validatePath` callers verified to degrade the new reason to their generic branch — none switch exhaustively).

Also: deletes the exports the move orphans (`isWithinAnyRoot`, `relativeFromRoot`, `normalizeAbsolute` — zero production callers), and fixes the stale "desktop-only" comment on `core-plugins.ts` (the plugin gate excludes android/ios and store builds; this code runs in cloud dedicated agents).

## What this lands

- **Mobile app-auth routes** — `GET /api/v1/app-auth/mobile/config`, `POST .../token`, `POST .../ack`, `GET/DELETE .../credentials[/:id]`, plus the `flow: "mobile_pkce"` branch on `POST /api/v1/app-auth/connect`. All fail closed behind `ELIZA_MOBILE_APP_AUTH_ENABLED === "true"` **and** a registered/approved `ELIZA_MOBILE_APP_AUTH_APP_ID`, so nothing is reachable until the deploy-time registration is provisioned (verifier script included: `packages/scripts/cloud/admin/verify-mobile-app-auth-registration.ts`).
- **S256 PKCE grant lifecycle** — one-time authorization codes bound to code_challenge/state/redirect; migrations renumbered from the stale 0177–0179 to **0269–0271** with the journal extended (develop had advanced to 0268).
- **Inactive-until-exact-ACK credentials** — `eliza_mobile_` secrets are minted inactive and excluded from every positive auth cache; only the exact ACK activates them; expiry, tombstone-based self/account revocation with durable receipts, and recovery listings are covered by the ported service + repository suites.
- **Ingress protection** — new `MOBILE_API_KEY_INGRESS_LIMITER` Cloudflare rate-limit binding (fresh namespace ids 1615304/1615314/1615324 — develop had already consumed the ids the draft used), credential-scoped limiter keys that never embed the secret, a global IP backstop on the dedicated-agent proxy fast path, and hard rejection of mobile secrets on the query/WebSocket transport.
- **Cleanup cron** — `/api/cron/cleanup-mobile-app-auth` on the existing `*/15` schedule drains expired grants and stale inactive credentials.

78:Tbb9,## Summary

Adds a first-party **Settings → Devices & Runtimes** experience for controlling account-owned Eliza runtimes from iPhone and desktop clients.

- pairs trusted controllers using QR deep links or six-digit one-use codes
- exposes local Mac, Eliza Cloud, linked desktop, and advanced SSH/VPS runtime targets
- relays signed, end-to-end encrypted commands through Eliza Cloud
- keeps SSH keys and VPS bearer credentials in native secure storage
- uses the owning Mac as the SSH gateway for VPS runtimes
- supports the existing Headscale path while retaining an encrypted Cloud-mailbox fallback
- adds host revocation, replay resistance, route allowlisting, credential migration, and runtime switching

## Security model

- pairing challenges expire after five minutes and are single-use
- controller and host identities are device-bound
- Cloud stores verifiers and opaque encrypted envelopes, not pairing codes or command plaintext
- SSH runs without a shell, binds forwarded ports to loopback, remembers first-seen host keys, and rejects changed keys
- untrusted authorization headers and non-agent routes are rejected
- scanned iOS pairing codes wait until Cloud authentication completes instead of being consumed prematurely

See `packages/app-core/docs/devices-runtimes-security.md` for the complete boundary.

# Background

## What does this PR do?

- Adds a dedicated manifest-v3 backup-catalog daemon with cadence bounded to at
  most 60 seconds, retry metrics, redacted health, and bounded shutdown.
- Composes the existing scheduler/catalog, authenticated Agent capture, KMS key
  bundles, affinity-aware durable spool, native R2 primary, Hetzner S3
  secondary, publication/verification, retention, deletion, and GC paths.
- Hardens runtime authority, cancellation, deadline, response-loss replay,
  partial-spool cleanup, exact provider deletion, and catalogue settlement.
- Adds a strict atomic systemd EnvironmentFile helper and fail-safe deployment:
  stop/disable old authority before safe-off replacement, install helper/unit
  through exact-SHA root-owned candidates, verify effective unit identity,
  fragment, drop-ins, and ExecStart before enabling.
- Keeps periodic admission and worker runtime disabled by default and forced off
  by deployment. It does not enroll the fleet, activate credentials, remove the
  legacy writer, mutate a live provider, or advertise an RPO.

- Adds ScenarioBackgroundRuntime start/pause/resume/step/drain/crash/restart/inspect/reset controls, typed ledger, error/readiness reporting, quiescence, per-agent reset, and external production-driver boundary.
- Adds declared worker/service/task-row readiness to scenario manifests and retains background evidence in reports.
- Injects TaskService time into plugin-scheduling standalone ticks and the LifeOps worker.
- Exercises the actual proactive handler, scheduling notification path, and Discord install-welcome Cloud queue.

`packages/ui/package.json` `exports` declares wildcard subpath entry points (`./cloud/*`, `./cloud-ui/*`, `./components/*`, `./api/*`, `./state/*`, `./agent-surface/*`, `./views/*`, `./bridge/*`, `./first-run/*`, `./platform/*`, `./slots/*`, `./utils/*`, `./services/*`). The build (`tsc -p tsconfig.build.json`, `include: ["src"]`) emits one `dist/<prefix>/...` output file per non-test, non-story source file under each prefix — with no dead-code elimination at the package boundary — so every one of those files is a genuine, externally-reachable public module (`@elizaos/ui/cloud/instances/components/docker-logs-viewer`, etc.), whether or not anything inside this monorepo imports it.

`packages/ui/scripts/audit-public-api.mjs` only ever checked `getExportsOfModule()` on `src/index.ts` — the root barrel. It had no visibility into this wildcard subpath surface at all. That is what let #23336 delete Cloud dashboard components (`docker-logs-viewer.tsx`, `account-limits-card.tsx`) with a clean in-repo-importer search: the deletion had zero in-repo importers, so it looked free, but the audit that should have caught a public-API narrowing structurally could not see this surface to begin with.

## What changed

- `audit-public-api.mjs` now also enumerates every `"./<prefix>/*" -> "./dist/<prefix>/*.js"` wildcard in `package.json` `exports`, resolves each back to its `src/<prefix>` source directory, and walks it (excluding `.test.ts(x)` / `.stories.ts(x)` / `.d.ts`, matching the build's own excludes) to produce public specifiers like `@elizaos/ui/cloud/billing/components/auto-top-up-card`.
- These are recorded in a new, separate `subpathExports` array in the baseline (`packages/ui/scripts/public-api-baseline.json`), diffed the same way as root exports — an added **or** removed subpath entry point fails the gate, same as a root export change.
- Root-export behavior, comparison logic, and the baseline's existing `exports` field are unchanged.
- `--update-baseline` regenerates both `exports` and `subpathExports`.

## Baseline diff summary

Regenerated against current `develop` (this repo already contains #23336's merged deletions):

- **143 root exports** — unchanged from before this PR.
- **1389 subpath entry points**, newly captured, spanning: `cloud` (272), `cloud-ui` (102), `components` (673), `api` (68), `state` (116), `first-run` (29), `services` (30), `platform` (22), `utils` (47), `agent-surface` (15), `bridge` (10), `views` (3), `slots` (2).
- `docker-logs-viewer` and `account-limits-card` are **already absent** from `develop` (#23336 merged before this branch), and correctly do not appear anywhere in the regenerated baseline. This PR does not restore them — it makes their removal (and any future one like it) visible to the gate.
