Fixes #19899

## What

Adds two first-party provider adapter plugins, modeled on the `plugin-google-workspace` connector pattern, projecting Notion and Dropbox into the notes/documents/files capabilities. Both speak the provider REST APIs directly over fetch — no MCP runtime, per the parent epic (#19877) architecture.

### `@elizaos/plugin-notion`
- `NotionClient` (API 2022-06-28): workspace search with cursor pagination, page reads, paginated block-children reads flattened to plain text (with unsupported-block-type reporting), page creation, paragraph appends. Every read result carries the canonical `notion.so` deep link for citations.
- Typed error surface: `NOTION_AUTH_EXPIRED` / `NOTION_FORBIDDEN` / `NOTION_NOT_FOUND` / `NOTION_RATE_LIMITED` (+`retryAfterSeconds`) / `NOTION_INVALID_REQUEST` / `NOTION_MALFORMED_RESPONSE` / `NOTION_UPSTREAM_FAILURE` — callers branch on codes, never HTTP details.
- OAuth: workspace-bound authorization-code flow (`owner=user`, Basic-auth token exchange — Notion has no PKCE, refresh tokens, or incremental scopes; access is scoped by what the user shares with the connection inside Notion's consent UI). Workspace identity (id/name/icon/owner) is recorded on the account for deterministic account selection.
- Credential resolution: BYO `NOTION_TOKEN` (local/self-hosted mode) → metadata credential refs → connector-account storage → vault refs.

### `@elizaos/plugin-dropbox`
- `DropboxClient` (API v2): `list_folder`(+`/continue`), `search_v2`(+`search/continue_v2`), `get_metadata`, `download`/`upload` via the content host with ASCII-escaped `Dropbox-API-Arg`, `get_temporary_link`. Deterministic `dropbox.com` deep links (folder browse / file preview) on every entry for citations.
- File limitation UX: `downloadText` refuses binary (`DROPBOX_FILE_NOT_TEXT`) and oversized (`DROPBOX_FILE_TOO_LARGE`, 1 MB cap, checked before download) files instead of returning garbage — callers offer `getTemporaryLink` instead. Uploads default to `mode: "add"` so accidental overwrites fail.
- OAuth: PKCE + `token_access_type=offline`. Default scope set = read scopes (`account_info.read`, `files.metadata.read`, `files.content.read`) plus the explicit write-escalation pair (`files.metadata.write`, `files.content.write`); caller-supplied scopes are normalized, unrecognized/empty selections fail closed; granted scopes are recorded on the account.
- Credential resolution adds refresh handling for Dropbox's short-lived tokens: refresh grant with a skew window, in-memory caching per account, refresh rejection surfaced as `DROPBOX_AUTH_EXPIRED`.

### Shared
- Durable token persistence reuses the provider-agnostic `persistConnectorCredentialRefs` helper (subpath import from `@elizaos/plugin-google-workspace/connector-credential-refs`) — tokens land in the vault/credential store as refs, never in account metadata, logs, or error contexts (asserted by tests).
- Both plugins register a `Service` (`runtime.getService("notion"|"dropbox")`) and a `ConnectorAccountProvider` at init; runtimes without a ConnectorAccountManager still get the service in BYO local mode.
- `registry-entry.json` for both, aggregated into `packages/registry/src/first-party/generated.json` via `generate:first-party`.
- Per-plugin `CLAUDE.md`/`AGENTS.md` (byte-identical, parity gate green) and `README.md`.
- Mock base-URL overrides (`ELIZA_MOCK_NOTION_BASE`, `ELIZA_MOCK_DROPBOX_BASE`, `ELIZA_MOCK_DROPBOX_CONTENT_BASE`) for protocol-faithful mock servers.

# What does this PR do?

- forwards the active action-turn signal into the public skill installer and preserves typed failures in `ActionResult`;
- owns request/response/socket disconnect cancellation across both slug routes, from before `isInstalled` through discovery, state publication, and response;
- stages discovered state and prevents late transport or state writes after disconnect;
- accepts every positive finite timeout and schedules values above Node's timer ceiling in monotonic segments;
- cancels every unused non-success body without masking the authoritative HTTP result, while reporting teardown failures;
- adds real peer-close coverage for catalog details/package and GitHub `SKILL.md`/README.

This preserves the existing boolean installer compatibility unless a caller explicitly requests typed errors.

# Risks

Medium. This changes cancellation and deadline ownership across action and HTTP install entry points. First-reason semantics, listener cleanup, discovery/state fencing, rejected-body teardown, and all remote legs have adversarial coverage.

# Documentation

The package README and paired `CLAUDE.md`/`AGENTS.md` document the positive-finite segmented timeout and caller-cancellation contract.

# What this fixes

- Aborts an in-flight Android Cloud login when the user cancels instead of allowing a late poll, credential write, browser operation, or session/history restore to authenticate the shell.
- Makes acknowledgement-required credential delivery atomic: the exact session-bound key is deactivated before plaintext reveal and activated only in the same primary transaction as receipt acknowledgement.
- Gives new CLI keys an exact `eliza_cli_<64 hex>` identity, bypasses positive API-key/inference caches, and revalidates them from the primary so neither pre-ACK use nor a stale cache refill can authenticate.
- Persists a non-authenticating provisional credential before ACK. Response loss, revocation failure, and process restart retain exact cleanup ownership; simultaneous quarantine/revocation failure is neutralized locally when possible.
- Stores an enumerable multi-record credential journal so failed A cleanup cannot be overwritten by B, rejects malformed journals without altering secure-store bytes, and retains exact response-loss receipts until revocation is confirmed.
- Serializes attempt-owned secure credential mutations so stale A cannot clear, acknowledge, or revoke newer B, and exposes PATCH/DELETE through the thin CLI-session dispatcher without capturing authenticated `/complete`.
- Rejects HEAD before the single-use reveal path, serializes ACK and cleanup through session/key row locks, and retains authenticated revocation receipts until their bound key expires or is deleted.
- Uses attempt-scoped voice ownership, retries teardown after a late native start settles, retains failed listener/removal handles, and binds every generated recognizer callback to its exact instance and epoch so stale A cannot notify or stop B.
- Translates native Android recognition codes into actionable recovery guidance while preserving terminal teardown and visible listening-state reset.
- Adds deterministic regressions across secure-store failure/relaunch, response-loss ACK/revoke, concurrent cancel/ack, cache refill, shared-runtime/inference ingress, browser-close hangs, late voice start, recognizer error, and teardown failure.

# Risks

Medium. This adds a public scenario-runner mutation/reset API. # Background

## What does this PR do?

- Validates a versioned synthetic manifest completely before writes, rejecting unsupported versions, unknown fields, duplicate IDs/pairs, bad references, wrong owners, and unsupported domain categories.
- Applies worlds, entities, rooms, participants, memories, relationships, and tasks through the real `IAgentRuntime` production CRUD boundaries. There is no parallel `WorldData` store.
- Uses deterministic namespace IDs where production contracts accept caller IDs. For SQL relationships, it deliberately ignores the non-authoritative batch return and records the persisted ID from `getRelationshipsByPairs()` readback.
- Returns a JSON-serializable receipt containing the exact created identifiers. Apply failure compensates and proves absence when possible; an ambiguous relationship outcome returns `SCENARIO_MANIFEST_DIRTY` with the receipt instead of claiming rollback.
- Projects a stable canonical snapshot from production stores, verifies receipt ownership before reset, supports idempotent/concurrent reset convergence, and proves byte-equivalent reset/reseed readback.
- Documents that schedules, notifications, approvals, and provider state remain unsupported until their existing production services/readback contracts are integrated.

## What kind of change is this?

Feature: a non-breaking scenario-runner persistence foundation.

# Documentation changes needed?

The scenario-runner README now documents the supported v1 boundary, receipt/reset contract, and explicit unsupported categories.

8d:T196e,Refs #22550 (does not close it — see "Human-only remainder" below)

## What this changes

The Worker built the entire application on every cold isolate. `bootstrap-app.ts` statically imported `_router.generated.ts`, which statically imported **all 677 route modules** before `createApp()` mounted anything — so the `appPromise` memoisation at `index.ts:188` was memoising work that had already been paid at module-evaluation time.

This implements the design the issue's attribution pointed at: **sharding the generated route graph behind lazy imports**, not a fifth thin shell and not matcher optimisation.

- `_generate-router.mjs` now emits each route as a lazy `() => import(...)` tagged with a **shard key** — the first literal segment after `/api` (or after `/api/v1` for the v1 tree). 677 routes → 126 shards.
- `createApp({ requestPath })` mounts only the shard that can match that path. `createApp()` (no argument) still mounts the whole tree for tests, the dev server, and any dispatch with no concrete path.
- `index.ts` memoises **one app per shard** instead of one per isolate, so a login request evaluates its own route family instead of all 677 modules.

## Why this is safe

- **Middleware and mount semantics are unchanged.** Sharding only filters *which* mounts get registered; each one is still an ordinary `app.route()`. Parent auth and request variables are preserved — deliberately not `app.mount()`, which would create a child `Context` and drop them (the hazard @lalalune flagged).
- **Mount order is preserved** within a shard, so static-before-dynamic precedence still holds.
- **Shard-key correctness is proven by construction**: a mount pattern and any request it can match share the literal segments the key is derived from. A `:param` or splat at the shard position yields `null`, meaning "mount into every shard". This is asserted over the real 677-mount table.
- **Process-global wiring** (audit dispatcher, apps-deploy triggers) is hoisted behind a once-per-isolate guard. Without it, building a second shard would replace a dispatcher that in-flight requests already hold — a regression this PR introduces the guard *and* a test for.

## Tests

New `src/router-shards.test.ts` exercises the real generated mount table:

- both `routeShardKey` implementations (runtime TS + codegen `.mjs`) agree on every one of the 677 mount paths and on representative request paths — they cannot silently drift;
- every mount's stored shard matches what `routeShardKey` derives;
- **dispatch equivalence**: for every one of the 677 mounts, a shard-filtered router resolves the same route as the full router (stub sub-apps, so no route module is evaluated);
- unmatched paths still 404 identically.

Plus, in `bootstrap-app.test.ts`: a shard-scoped app mounts its own family and not others while retaining the manually-registered routes, and the once-per-isolate wiring test above.

```
bun test src/bootstrap-app.test.ts src/index.test.ts src/router-shards.test.ts
  62 pass, 0 fail (3707 expect() calls)

bun test __tests__/bootstrap-app-unhandled-error.test.ts __tests__/oidc-provider.test.ts
  133 pass, 0 fail

node test/_router-contract.mjs
  {"mountedRoutes":677,"checked":["inventory parity","static-before-dynamic ordering",
   "named catch-all conversion","method dispatch","trailing slash compatibility"]}

bunx tsc --noEmit    exit 0
biome check          no fixes applied
bun run check:agents-claude    PASS (157 pairs byte-identical)
```

Route count is unchanged at 677 and `_router-contract.mjs` still asserts inventory parity, so no route was dropped. The four route-graph parsers (`_router-contract`, `_inventory`, `_audit-coverage`, `_frontend-gaps`) were updated for the new generated shape; `_audit-coverage` still reports `Mounted: 677`.

Codegen now pre-wraps over-80-column `load:` lines the way Biome would, so `bun run codegen` and `bun run lint` no longer reformat each other's output (verified: regenerate → format → zero diff).

## Human-only remainder — this PR does NOT close the issue's proofs

The issue's Definition of Done requires before/after measurements taken **from the same colo, same client, same time window, against a deployed Worker**, with the cold-isolate floor published separately from the graph-construction win. **None of that can be established from this PR**, and I am explicitly not claiming it:

- **Proof 1** (three-line decomposition), **Proof 2** (full-app median from outside), **Proof 3** (thin/full gap), **Proof 4** (no return of startup error 10021) all require a staged Cloudflare deployment plus external timing. The blocker named by @lalalune — authorization/access for a staged Worker deploy and same-colo observability — is unchanged by this PR.
- Local timings are **not** evidence here. The test suite got faster (18s → 12s) once shard-scoped apps replaced full-tree mounts, which is consistent with the mechanism but is a Bun-resolution artifact, not a latency claim.
- Per the issue: do **not** credit sign-in completion rate as the payoff; it is burst-shaped and will recover on its own.

One trade-off a reviewer should weigh: an isolate serving many distinct path families now builds several middleware stacks instead of one (matcher construction is single-digit ms each, per the prior audit), in exchange for evaluating only the route modules a request can actually reach. If the deploy window shows that trade landing badly for spray traffic, the shard granularity (currently first literal segment) is the dial to turn.

<!-- eliza-computer-attribution:v1 {"provider":"openai","model":"gpt-5.6-sol","client":"Codex Desktop","skill_revision":"elizaOS/eliza@31679563771bac5f3f1b18d9cf6eafc99c3f71ae:packages/skills/skills/contribute-to-eliza"} -->8f:T14ca,## PR3 of the split-disclosure series: wire min-over-members admission into the EGRESS seam

Third PR of the smart per-recipient split-response disclosure series (design: `W1-SPLIT-DISCLOSURE-SCOPE-2026-08-21`). PR1 (#23813) shipped the pure policy core (`resolveAudienceAdmission`); this PR wires it into the **output/delivery** seam. It is deliberately **distinct from `DisclosureGate`** (the input/composition gate a sibling lane wires): `DisclosureGate` gates whether a provider/action *runs and enters the prompt* (`action-gate.ts` / `runtime.ts`); this seam gates what *leaves* at delivery time (`enforceTrustedDeliveryAudienceAtEgress` in `services/message.ts`).

### What this adds

**`packages/core/src/access-control/audience-egress.ts`** — the ONE place the egress path builds the per-viewer resolver the policy core requires, so the delivery seam never hand-rolls a per-member `AccessContext`:

- `viewerResolverFromAudience(subject, audience)` — derived PURELY from attested evidence (`TrustedDeliveryAudience`), no room reads / no entity-role I/O in the hot delivery path. The canonical owner (`canonicalOwnerEntityId`) resolves as `OWNER` (unconditional `full`); every other participant gets the bare least-privileged `USER` tier, so the artifact grant/scope ladder decides — a `full` grant elevates, a `redacted` grant narrows, the `owner-private` default fails closed to `none`. This is the fail-closed floor: attestation proves who is in the room, not what elevated world-role a non-owner might hold, so a non-owner is admitted only what an explicit grant or an open scope allows. The resolver is built EXACTLY the way PR1 mandates: `resolveArtifactDisclosure` over `disclosureSubjectRecord(subject)`.
- `resolveEgressAudienceAdmission(subject, audience)` — thin, fail-closed composition over the pure policy core.
- `parseEgressDisclosureSubject(value)` — fail-closed parser for the `content.data.disclosureSubject` marker: an unknown scope or a present-but-non-object marker collapses to `owner-private` (a corrupt marker can only narrow, never widen); malformed grant entries are dropped (never a fabricated grant); only a fully **absent** marker means "unscoped".

**Egress wiring in `services/message.ts`:**

- `enforceTrustedDeliveryAudienceAtEgress` now runs the audience-admission check FIRST. A response that declares its disclosure subject is joined with the REAL attested audience; anything short of a `full` min-over-members admission is withheld with the `PRIVACY_DENIED` shape carrying `privacyReason: audience_admission:<level>`. A withholding short-circuits the owner-exclusive revalidation (its replacement carries no owner-private data). Both seams are independent and both fail closed.
- `enforceTrustedDeliveryAudienceOnResult` no longer early-returns for a turn that did not consume owner-private data when the response declares a disclosure subject, so the actions-mode multi-memory rewrite covers audience-admission withholdings too.

Exported from the node/browser/edge barrels (type-only `TrustedDeliveryAudience` import keeps it browser-safe, matching `audience-disclosure`).

### Explicitly NOT in this PR

`DisclosureGate` and its enforcement (`types/components.ts`, `runtime/action-gate.ts`, `runtime.ts`, `security/trusted-delivery-audience.ts`) are **untouched** — the sibling PR2 owns that. `git diff --name-only` = 3 new files + `services/message.ts` + the three barrels only.

### Tests (bidirectional)

**`message.egress-audience-admission.test.ts`** (4 tests, REAL attested audiences via `attestDeliveryAudienceFromCanonicalRoom` — never a cast):

- **PASS direction:** an owner-only DM whose census admits `full` delivers the scoped response untouched.
- **FAIL-WITHOUT direction (bidirectional proof):** a GROUP room with an ungranted stranger caps the subject to `none`; the seam replaces the scoped response with the denial and rewrites every response memory. **Verified this exact assertion FAILS on the pre-wiring seam** (stashed the `services/message.ts` wiring: the scoped `SCOPED_LEAK_…` canary shipped in full because the seam early-returned unless `ownerExclusiveDisclosureWasUsed`).
- fail-closed: a declared subject with NO attested audience is withheld; an unscoped response (no marker) is untouched.

**`audience-egress.test.ts`** (16 tests): resolver tiers (owner→full, non-owner→ladder, grant-beats-ladder both directions, null-owner floor), admission composition, and the fail-closed subject parser.

# Background

## What does this PR do?

- Defines the versioned core identity vocabulary: account-scoped claims, canonical redirects, merge/split plans, confirmations, journals, delivery resolution, and discriminated owner-binding decisions.
- Adds portable schema descriptors and real Drizzle tables with composite tenant FKs, immutable journal evidence, generation fencing, phase-specific idempotency, and active-only scoped-claim uniqueness.
- Implements a SQL identity service using one real Drizzle transaction for confirm/commit/split, preserving source principals and claims rather than destructively rewriting them.
- Removes generic confirmed `identity_link` inheritance from OWNER and manual private-access role resolution. The temporary compatibility path accepts only connector IDs carrying the verified owner-pairing marker.
- Hardens owner evaluation to require a connected, non-deleted account, matching connector, matching external subject, matching runtime instance, and a verified binding. Configured owner aliases are canonicalized.
- Keeps the service exported but cutover-gated until claim lifecycle/backfill and authenticated merge consumers land.

Feature foundation plus security hardening; non-breaking public additions, with intentionally stricter privilege resolution for generic relationship links.

# Risks

Medium, constrained by a hard dormant boundary:

- This adds DB authority and callback-scoped secret-opening primitives, but deliberately adds no production caller or top-level export.
- The current node-history schema has no durable occurrence token. This PR therefore fails closed for any node record that has ever carried a different non-null incarnation. A separate occurrence-token migration is required before activation; this PR does not claim general ABA-safe node reuse.
- `allocated_count` ownership is not durable across shared reconciliation. The boundary must not be lifted until shared allocator ownership, settlement/release, and anti-double-count integration land in coordination with #22916.
- The vault callback is trusted, bounded, fully awaited, remote-only, and must honor its `AbortSignal`; it must not re-enter the locked DB authority.
- No migration, real KMS call, SSH, container operation, provisioning, autoscale, routing change, or deployment is introduced.

# Background

## What does this PR do?

- Reserves one caller-selected existing Docker node record and exact incarnation under a live restore claim, lease, and catalogue epoch.
- Uses the canonical multi-authority order backup → operation → lease → node → immutable node history → catalogue, then reads the primary DB clock after the final lock.
- Validates the target image against the canonical manifest-v3 digest and persists node record, incarnation, and image digest in the same transaction as the capacity CAS.
- Makes response-loss replay idempotent and rejects divergence, stale catalogue authority, invalid claims/leases, saturated or provisional nodes, target reselection, autoscale, and environment fallback.
- Keeps cross-backup restore-attempt divergence out of the blocking lease lock, closing the catalogue/lease deadlock found by the real PostgreSQL proof.
- Prevents the generic phase-advance API from writing target identity or leaving `reserved` without the complete target triplet.
- Proves the exact target before KMS unwrap, re-proves it after KMS, and executes the trusted byte callback while the second authority transaction still holds its locks. The handoff has a 1–60 second bound, a 1 second lease/claim margin, cooperative cancellation, post-callback DB-clock proof, and synchronous zeroization.
- Rejects any immutable history for a different incarnation on the selected node record. This conservative rule is intentionally availability-reducing until the occurrence-token migration lands.
- Keeps every new API definition-only until durable allocation ownership and quarantined creation are ready.

## What kind of change is this?

Feature: non-breaking, dormant repository authority for the next #20732 slice.

# Documentation changes needed?

No user-facing documentation change is needed because the API remains definition-only. The integration prohibitions are documented in JSDoc and enforced by the boundary test.

94:T16ba,## Summary

Implements the codeable-now scope of #19903: a provider-neutral design domain package (`@elizaos/plugin-design`) with real local-mode **Figma** and **Canva** provider adapters, read/search-first per the issue, while managed Cloud OAuth stays an explicit, typed eligibility-gated state until provider app approval.

### What's included

- **Normalized design domain** (`src/types.ts`): validated `DesignRef` / `DesignPage` / `DesignExportArtifact` / `DesignCommentPage` contracts; deep links and thumbnails must be HTTPS, Canva links pinned to `canva.com`.
- **Bounded transport core** (`src/http.ts`): one pinned origin, core `fetchWithSsrfGuard` DNS-pinned transport, no redirects, bounded deadlines and response bytes, strict schema decoding, adapter-supplied provider error classification. Modeled on the merged `plugin-maps` adapter from the same epic.
- **`FigmaDesignAdapter`** (`src/figma.ts`): real Figma REST wire — `/v1/projects/:id/files` (search; designed-unpaginated), `/v1/files/:key`, `/v1/images/:key` node renders, `/v1/files/:key/comments` — BYO `X-Figma-Token` personal access token (local mode; `FIGMA_API_BASE_URL` supports a local desktop-bridge/test origin).
- **`CanvaDesignAdapter`** (`src/canva.ts`): real Canva Connect wire — `/rest/v1/designs` with continuation cursors, `/rest/v1/designs/:id`, async export job create + bounded polling — BYO Connect access token. Comment reads and SVG export are typed `DESIGN_UNSUPPORTED` (Canva beta/paid capability), not fabricated empties; paid/beta provider codes map to `DESIGN_PLAN_LIMITED`.
- **`DesignService`** (`src/service.ts`): adapter registry, capability routing on typed `capabilities` sets, provider identity binding on every response, settings-driven local-mode startup, no silent Cloud fallback (`DESIGN_NOT_CONNECTED`), and `MANAGED_DESIGN_ELIGIBILITY` + `connectManaged` throwing `DESIGN_MANAGED_MODE_INELIGIBLE`.
- Typed `DesignError` codes distinguish expired vs revoked vs plan-limited auth, rate limit (with `retryAfterMs`), timeout, network, endpoint-blocked, oversized, malformed, and export failure.

### Tests (deterministic, protocol-faithful — not mocks of the system under test)

Both adapters run the repository's managed-provider conformance harness (`@elizaos/cloud-test-mocks/provider-contract`) over real HTTP against the fake upstream speaking Figma/Canva wire shapes:

- Figma: full 13-scenario `outbound-http` matrix; Canva: 14 with `pagination`.
- Expired / revoked / plan-limited auth distinctions per provider.
- Canva async export lifecycle: success, failed job, plan-limited job, stuck-job polling budget.
- Figma render failures (`err`, null image URLs), missing-file 404 → null, nodeId requirement.
- SSRF/private-origin/userinfo/query endpoint rejection, DNS-rebinding block, redirect refusal, response byte bounds, provider identity spoof rejection, off-domain deep-link rejection, secret redaction, opaque connection ids.
- `DesignService` registry/routing/binding/eligibility/settings suite.

## Summary

Adds the durable persistence foundation for the $30/month Plus and $100/month Pro subscription program:

- canonical tenant-scoped subscription lifecycle rows plus immutable revisions
- rebuildable organization entitlement projections with explicit free backfill
- non-rollover allowance periods with overlap prevention
- append-only allowance ledger with reserve, settle, refund, expire, clawback, and audited close transitions
- exact allowance/purchased-credit funding reservation splits
- primary-only repositories with tenant locks, CAS, provider-version fencing, and exact idempotent replay

This intentionally does not add Stripe mutation routes, mixed-source debit orchestration, or UI. Those remain in #23092-#23097. Plan values and provider bindings remain server-owned by #23090.

## Safety invariants

- purchased credit balance is never mutated by these migrations
- allowance refunds after expiry remain in the expired audit bucket
- cross-tenant and cross-period references are rejected by composite FKs and repository checks
- lifecycle revisions and allowance transactions are append-only
- one live subscription per organization and non-overlapping allowance periods are database-enforced
- free entitlement projections cascade with organization deletion; paid lifecycle authority remains explicit

## What

Builds the routed `/maps` web view for `@elizaos/plugin-maps`, following the established plugin-notes view architecture:

- **View declaration + app-shell registration** — `mapsPlugin.views` declares the `maps` view (`/maps`, OWNER role gate, `dist/views/bundle.js`, `MapsView` export, MAPS action affinity); `src/register.ts` + `elizaos.appRegister` register the lazy page in the signed app bundle, discovered by the manifest scan (expected-list test updated, `@elizaos/plugin-maps` added as an app workspace dep).
- **Read-only capability broker** — `MAPS_VIEW_CAPABILITIES` (`get-maps-state`, `search-places`, `get-place`, `plan-route-alternatives`, `get-saved-places`) dispatch through `serverInteract` against the real `MapsService`. Saved-place writes stay on the promoted `MAPS_SAVE` action so receipt settlement is never bypassed. Expected domain failures (invalid input, provider unavailable, not found, auth expired/revoked, rate limited) become explicit `success: false` results; systemic failures propagate to the route boundary.
- **State boundary** — `GET /api/maps/state` returns the validated snapshot DTO (providers with required attribution, provider availability, owner-scoped saved places). A missing owner entity is an explicit `unavailable` state, never a healthy-looking empty list.
- **Shared zod contract** — `src/view-contract.ts` (runtime-import-free) is parsed by both the server producer and the browser transport, so malformed payloads are rejected instead of rendered.
- **Browser bundle** — responsive map/list grid; deterministic SVG map pane (polyline decode + equirectangular viewBox projection); place details; route alternatives across all four travel modes with explicit per-mode failure rows; category filter chips; cursor pagination; saved places; attribution footer. Orange accent only. Keyboard/screen-reader coverage: labelled search form, aria-pressed filters/results, focusable SVG markers with Enter/Space activation, role=alert errors, aria-live loading.
- **Distinct states** — loading, designed-empty, transport error, offline (online/offline listeners pause search/routing), and provider-unavailable each render differently.
- **Adapter surface (additive)** — optional `MapsProviderAdapter.attribution`, `MapsService.describeProviders()`.
- **Unblocking fix** — removed duplicate `desktopHttpTransportForUrl`/`fetchAgentTransport` imports in `packages/ui/src/api/client-cloud.ts` (TS2300 on develop) that failed every plugin typecheck that path-maps `@elizaos/ui`.

## What

Implements the core contract + store + engine + action slice for flexible daily quota routines ("25 pushups, 3 sets a day, doesn't matter when"):

- **Shared contract** (`packages/shared/src/contracts/personal-assistant.ts`): new `count_per_day` cadence variant (`targetCount`, `unit`, `perOccurrenceWork`, `timing`) with `LifeOpsQuotaTiming` — `anytime` is structurally distinct from windows/slots and deliberately has **no** `slots`. New `LifeOpsProgressEvent`, `LifeOpsOccurrenceProgress` (required `completedCount`/`targetCount`/`remainingCount`), `RecordLifeOpsProgressRequest/Result`, and the `occurrence_progress_recorded` audit event type. Fixed-slot `times_per_day` is untouched.
- **No more fabricated slots**: `buildDistributedDailySlots` is **deleted**. The count-only paths in `buildCadenceFromLlmParams` and `normalizeCadenceDetail` now emit the quota cadence (`anytime`, or `windows` timing when the owner named windows). Explicitly named times still produce fixed slots.
- **Engine** (`engine.ts`): exactly **one** owner-local active-day occurrence per local date (`quota:<localDateKey>:day`) spanning the owner's day in the definition timezone (or the union of named windows). Next-day reset falls out of the per-day occurrence key; terminal states stay sticky; `derivedTarget` carries the quota descriptor.
- **Persistence**: new append-only `app_lifeops.life_task_progress_events` table (drizzle-pushed via the existing plugin `schema` map; plain text columns, no pg enums) with `unique(agent_id, occurrence_id, idempotency_key)`. Repository adds `appendProgressEventIfNew` (single-statement `INSERT … ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING RETURNING`, mirroring `createAuditEventIfNew`), `sumProgressEvents`, `listProgressEvents`. The completed count is always re-derived from the event table — never cached on the occurrence row, so full-row occurrence upserts cannot clobber concurrent progress.
- **Service** (`definitions-service.ts` / `service.ts`): `recordOccurrenceProgress(occurrenceId, {idempotencyKey, quantity?, note?})` — idempotent append, transactional-safety via the unique constraint, completion through the existing retry-idempotent `completeOccurrence` exactly when the derived count reaches the target (streaks/performance/website-access/escalation flow unchanged), 409 from skipped/expired/muted, refusal after completion, count clamped at target in the projection.
- **Chat path** (`life.ts`): on a `count_per_day` occurrence, "I did one set" (the `complete` operation) records ONE increment keyed `msg:<message.id>` — a replayed/re-planned turn never double-counts — and replies with server-projected counts ("Logged 1/3 sets — 2 to go" / "3/3 — done for today"); target reached terminal-completes. `summarizeCadence` renders the quota honestly ("25 pushups 3 sets a day, any time") instead of fabricated `Time 1/2/3` labels. Quota definitions skip the default offset-0 reminder step (it would fire at local midnight since the occurrence starts at day start).

# Background

## What does this PR do?

Adds a consumer-first observation boundary that wraps existing connector,
repository, service, or use-case entry points. It records sanitized canonical
request/response/readback hashes, generation, idempotency identity, worker/task
retry lineage, typed acceptance, injected-clock timestamps, and failure detail.

`succeeded` is impossible unless the real boundary call ran, returned an
accepted result, authoritative readback exists and matches, and the active
generation is still current. Timeout, retryable/permanent, rate-limit, partial,
ambiguous, and stale-completion scripts all fail without fabricated success.

The integration proof wraps the production scheduling
`dispatchViaMessageConnector` path and classifies its typed `DispatchResult`.
Restart proof reopens the same append-only ledger, preserves the prior
generation, rejects a stale completion, and continues ordering in the new one.

## What kind of change is this?

Feature (non-breaking scenario/evidence infrastructure).

# Documentation changes needed?

Updated `packages/scenario-runner/README.md` with the authority boundary,
success/readback rule, fault contract, and #24076 single-writer prerequisite.

9f:T129c,Fixes #14758

## Summary

Fresh current-base vertical slice of the local-only, snapshot-consistent multi-account Gmail collector, built into the existing `packages/corpus-tools` collectors pattern (per the 2026-07-22 triage refresh, which cleared `needs-human` and re-scoped this as unclaimed implementation work). Addresses every gap flagged in the branch-cleanup audit of the deleted `feat/14758-gmail-corpus-collector` branch:

- **Real Gmail History reconciliation** — a completed checkpoint is never trusted indefinitely. Each subsequent run reconciles from the checkpointed `historyId` via `users.history.list`, applying additions and deletions; an expired/invalid history id (HTTP 404/400) triggers a full rescan instead of trusting the stale marker.
- **Account-namespaced ids** — `gmail:<account>:<messageId>` / `gmail:<account>:thread:<threadId>`; shards live under `gmail/<account>/<yyyy-mm>.jsonl`, and the transport's `getProfile` mailbox must match the requested account (`GMAIL_COLLECT_ACCOUNT_MISMATCH`) for account isolation.
- **Alias-aware direction** — `From` is compared against the account plus configured `aliasEmails`; the `SENT` label is also honored.
- **Locking / durable publication** — per-account fail-closed lock (`GMAIL_COLLECT_OUTPUT_BUSY`), atomic temp-file+rename installs, byte-compare idempotent shard reuse, validated `manifest.json` written last.
- **Enforced private output** — 0600 files and 0700 directories for shards, checkpoints, staging, and state.

Core collector semantics (`packages/corpus-tools/src/collectors/gmail.ts`):

- Injected `GmailTransport` seam (profile / paginated list / full message / attachment / history); the package holds no OAuth material. A live run wraps the existing account-scoped plugin-google Gmail client with `gmail.read` scope (adapter contract documented in the package README).
- Frozen UTC window expressed in **epoch seconds** (`after:<sec> before:<sec>`) because Gmail's `after:yyyy/mm/dd` is local-timezone and would shift the frozen cutoff; chats excluded, drafts dropped by label.
- Exhaustive pagination with a durable per-page checkpoint (`data/.state/gmail-<account>.json`) plus an append-only staging file, so an interrupted run resumes at the persisted page token without refetching staged mail; torn staging tails from a crash are dropped and refetched; excluded ids (drafts/out-of-window/attachment-only) are checkpointed so incremental runs do not refetch them forever.
- Bounded 429/5xx retries with exponential backoff honoring the server `Retry-After` hint.
- MIME extraction prefers `text/plain`, falls back to stripped `text/html`; attachment bytes are fetched only to compute SHA-256 + size; attachment-only messages are counted, never given fabricated text (audit rule).
- Deterministic dedup across pages/mutation; deleted messages cannot resurrect from stale staging (staging is compacted).
- Output committed by a schema-validated manifest; `validateCorpusTarget` passes on the produced tree.

No MBOX fallback was built, per the triage instruction (only if live API evidence establishes a real blocker).

## What

First work-integration native plugin adapter for epic #19877 wave 5. Adds `@elizaos/plugin-linear`, a read-only Linear plugin exposing elizaOS actions instead of an MCP wrapper:

- **`LinearClient`** (`src/client.ts`): bounded GraphQL-over-HTTPS client pinned to a single endpoint (`https://api.linear.app/graphql` by default). Uses core's DNS-pinned SSRF guard, rejects redirects/userinfo/query endpoints, enforces one deadline and one response byte limit per request. HTTP status classification stays authoritative; Linear's GraphQL error envelopes (`extensions.code`: `AUTHENTICATION_ERROR`, `FORBIDDEN`, `RATELIMITED`) refine auth/rate-limit classification — Linear reports auth failures on `400`, which is handled explicitly. Expired vs revoked credentials remain distinct typed failures; `429` retains `retryAfterMs`.
- **`LinearService`** (`src/service.ts`): credential resolution — managed `LINEAR_OAUTH_TOKEN` (Bearer) wins over BYO `LINEAR_API_KEY` (raw Authorization, per Linear's personal-key contract); neither configured fails with typed `LINEAR_NOT_CONFIGURED`, never a fabricated-empty page. Cloud's OAuth callback already whitelists `linear` as a provider platform.
- **Actions** (`src/action.ts` + `src/plugin.ts`): `LINEAR` umbrella promoted to `LINEAR_MY_ISSUES`, `LINEAR_SEARCH`, `LINEAR_ISSUE`, `LINEAR_TEAMS` via `promoteSubactionsToActions`, all tagged `domain:work` / `capability:read`. Search filters are built from typed parameters only (title/team/state/isMe), never prose. J1 boundary translation of `LinearError` with retryable/retry-after metadata.
- All response payloads are zod-validated (`src/types.ts`); workflow-state types are a closed enum and drift is rejected, not coerced.

## Read-only by design

Per the issue ("start read-only and enable writes incrementally"), no write action ships here — no stubs either. `plugins/plugin-linear/CLAUDE.md` pins the invariant: a write requires the epic's write-policy/receipt contracts.

# Risks

**Large identity/migration risk, dormant runtime exposure.** The migrations add a write-once occurrence-history authority to every Docker-node identity transition and bind restore operations to one exact history row. A bad constraint or lock order could block node/restore writers, so the change is split into three sub-100-line migrations and exercised against both PGlite and disposable real PostgreSQL. # Background

## What does this PR do?

- Appends migrations `0283`, `0284`, and `0285` after the current live journal tail.
- Adds immutable node-incarnation history and a trigger-owned current occurrence pointer. A real A1 → B → A2 transition produces distinct authorities even when the logical node record returns to A.
- Adds `expected_node_history_id` to restore-operation target identity and makes the full target tuple relationally exact and write-once.
- Carries the occurrence fence through reservation, vault seed, activation publication, and final receipt writers under the repository's global backup → operation → lease → sandbox → node → catalogue lock order.
- Preserves non-restore publication/replay/dispatch behavior while binding it to the same durable node record, incarnation, and history.

# Background

## What does this PR do?

`packages/core/src/runtime/schema-compat.ts` `normalizeSchemaForCerebras` is
the live Cerebras tool-schema walk used by `plugins/plugin-openai/models/text.ts`
`normalizeNativeToolsForCall` before a planner/chat hop. On origin `develop`
it recursed with `Object.entries` and no depth/cycle cap, so a cyclic `not`
graph RangeError'd and an 8k-deep `properties` nest that `JSON.parse` already
accepted then stack-overflowed the walk.

Earlier heads bounded depth/node/cycle/accessor reads with typed
`CEREBRAS_SCHEMA_UNBOUNDED`, moved every `Array.isArray` / `getPrototypeOf` /
array-length read inside `inspectSchema`, made cycle detection path-local so
honest DAGs pass, reserved width before allocation, and moved the bounded pass
in front of `sanitizeJsonSchema` so the raw-spread sanitizer can never see an
unbounded or hostile graph.

This head fixes the compatibility defect Shaw found in that ordering. The
pre-pass is now `cloneSchemaForBoundedTransport`: the same descriptor-only
reflection, path-local cycle detection, width-reserved clone, aggregate node
budget and typed failures, but zero Cerebras semantics. Running the full
normalizer there overwrote every declared `additionalProperties` (`true` or
schema-valued) with `false`, and `sanitizeJsonSchema` only builds
`__eliza_record_entries` plus a `RecordArgTransform` when
`additionalProperties !== false` — so a tool such as
`{ customFields: { type: "object", additionalProperties: { type: "string" } } }`
reached the wire as a closed empty object with no entries field and no reverse
mapping. Sanitization now sees a plain, budgeted graph with declared semantics
intact; `normalizeSchemaForCerebras` applies provider closure afterwards, as
on origin `develop`.

This head fixes the compatibility defect Shaw found in that clone. The clone
now mirrors `walkSchemaChildren` exactly — same keyword tables
(`SCHEMA_MAP_KEYS` / `SCHEMA_ARRAY_KEYS` / `SCHEMA_SINGLE_KEYS` / `items` /
`dependencies`), same guards, same depth accounting, same aggregate node budget
and path-local cycle detection — and never descends into annotation or
extension data, which is legal arbitrary JSON that neither the normalizer nor
`sanitizeJsonSchema` walks. Those values ride across in the immutable
descriptor snapshot, so no accessor runs and nothing is capped. Depth is now
counted in schema levels, so `MAX_CEREBRAS_SCHEMA_CLONE_DEPTH` is gone and the
pre-pass reports the same `MAX_CEREBRAS_SCHEMA_WALK_DEPTH` budget as the
normalizer. The clone still covers a superset of the keywords
`sanitizeJsonSchema` recurses into, so the sanitizer's raw
spread / `Object.entries` / `.map` recursion stays bounded.

The same pass collapses the remaining doubled descriptor reads: `ownDataEntries`
takes one immutable `{key, value}` snapshot per node and `cloneOwnData`,
`mapSchemaRecord`, `dependencies`, and the clone all consume it.

## What kind of change is this?

Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)

## Why are we doing this? Any context or related work?

See #23198 and Shaw's reviews on #23159. Cerebras mode must fail closed with a
typed cause instead of a `RangeError`/raw `TypeError`, must not change honest
programmatic DAG schemas, and must not silently collapse declared open maps
(#11249).

# Documentation changes needed?

My changes do not require a change to the project documentation.

# Risks

Medium, bounded by a definition-only API gate:

- No production caller or top-level export exists.
- The parent C1a schema still lacks a durable node-incarnation occurrence token. A separate migration is mandatory before activation.
- Restore capacity ownership is not durable across the shared allocator reconciler. Settlement/release and anti-double-count integration with #22916 are mandatory before activation.
- A future remote creator must be idempotent and reconcile or clean up a container when the database recorder rejects after a lease, catalogue, node, or placement drift.
- This PR contains no Docker/SSH/provider/registry call, no environment fallback, no migration, no route publication, and no deployment.

# Background

## What does this PR do?

- Opens a target activation quarantine only after the exact restore operation, claim, lease, manifest-v3 source, reserved node target, node history, and catalogue epoch are locked and re-proven.
- Derives the target activation generation from the retry-stable `restore_attempt_id`; callers cannot substitute the source generation or mint a second target identity.
- Writes only the mutable activation ledger. Canonical `sandbox_id`, `node_id`, `image_digest`, `status`, route publication, dispatch, and completion remain untouched.
- Records one already-created 64-character Docker container ID by atomically updating the quarantine ledger and the restore operation from `vault_seeded` to `container_created`, then clears the claim.
- Makes exact response-loss replay idempotent and rejects token, backup, claim, lease, catalogue, node-incarnation, placement, and container divergence without partial writes.
- Uses backup → operation → lease → sandbox → node → immutable node history → catalogue → DB-clock order.
- Removes the generic container-identity writer and blocks generic first entry into `container_created`. A retry may re-enter that phase only when the durable container ID already exists, and never rewrites it.
- Enforces a static definition-only boundary with no Docker provider, node manager, autoscaler, registry, SSH, `process.env`, or network import/call.

## What kind of change is this?

Feature: non-breaking, dormant repository authority for quarantined restore creation.

# Documentation changes needed?

No user-facing documentation change is needed because the API remains definition-only. JSDoc records the occurrence-token and allocation-settlement prerequisites.

a8:T1538,Fixes #19908 (epic #19877, integrations 6.3)

## What

Adds the integration reliability, cost, and release dashboard: an operator-facing surface exposing provider health, OAuth/webhook errors, costs, latency, stale sync, reauth demands, policy denies, release-evidence status, and kill switches — with no PII or secrets — plus the production account setup/runbook checklist.

### Domain read-model — `packages/cloud/shared/src/lib/integrations/reliability.ts`
- Typed telemetry contract (`IntegrationTelemetryEvent`, 7 kinds: capability_call, oauth_error, webhook_error, policy_deny, reauth_required, sync_completed, kill_switch_block) with strict boundary validation (`parseIntegrationTelemetryEvent`) throwing typed `IntegrationTelemetryValidationError` — explicit invalid results, never fake-valid defaults.
- Secret/PII redaction at ingest (`redactIntegrationDiagnostics`): Bearer/JWT/`sk-`/`ghp_`/`xox`/AKIA tokens, `key=value` credential pairs, emails, long hex/base64 entropy — plus a redaction-audit helper `findSecretLeaksInPayload` that scans finished payloads.
- `IntegrationTelemetryRecorder`: bounded, idempotent-per-event-id in-memory buffer (duplicate webhook deliveries/retries never double-count).
- Operator config parsers for `INTEGRATION_KILL_SWITCHES` and `INTEGRATION_RELEASE_EVIDENCE` env bindings — malformed entries surface in an explicit `invalid` list (error-policy:J3), never silently dropped.
- `buildIntegrationReliabilityDashboard`: pure, deterministic per-provider aggregation — error rate, p50/p95 latency, micro-USD cost totals, per-kind counts, stale-sync detection, kill-switch scope, evidence status, health classification (healthy/degraded/down/disabled/unknown) against an `IntegrationSloConfig`, and SLO breach alerts.
- `PRODUCTION_INTEGRATION_RUNBOOK`: the 8-item production account setup checklist, served with the dashboard and mirrored in `packages/cloud/shared/docs/integration-production-runbook.md`.

### API — `packages/cloud/api/v1/admin/integrations/reliability/route.ts`
- `GET /api/v1/admin/integrations/reliability` — super_admin-gated, rate-limited; returns `{dashboard, runbook, invalidConfig}`.

## What this adds

**plugin-maps (`plugins/plugin-maps`)**

## What

Adds `packages/core/src/capability-selection/`, building on the Wave 0 provider-integration contracts (`types/provider-integrations.ts`):

- **`retrieval.ts`** — deterministic capability retrieval over the normalized capability catalog (id/domain/keywords/summary — never provider or MCP schemas). Returns a bounded, relevance-ranked subset with prompt-flood metrics (`catalogPromptTokenEstimate` vs `retrievedPromptTokenEstimate`, `floodRatio`) and explicit cross-domain ambiguity reporting. Empty or non-matching intents yield a designed-empty result, never the full catalog.
- **`account-selection.ts`** — deterministic connected-account/adapter selection using policy (blocked accounts, allowed modes/providers, risk ceiling), health, region, and cost, with a fixed total order (region match → unit cost → recency → accountId). A pinned `requestedAccountId` is honored exactly or fails with a typed reason — an ineligible pinned account is never silently substituted (wrong-account prevention). Failures reuse the typed `CapabilityPolicyDenialCode` / `CapabilityUnavailableCode` contracts, and a policy denial takes precedence over mere unavailability.
- **`evaluation.ts` + `evaluation-corpus.ts`** — evaluation harness and built-in corpus (12 cases over a 10-capability representative catalog): unambiguous intents, ambiguous cross-domain intents, designed-empty intents, revoked/blocked/cost-blocked/unhealthy accounts, risk-policy denial, pinned-account prevention, and tie-break ordering. The report carries per-case latency and aggregate token/flood metrics.

Exported from `index.node.ts`.

# Background

## What does this PR do?

`packages/agent/src/services/character-history.ts` `toCharacterHistoryValue`
is the live snapshot walk for `PUT /api/character` (`buildCharacterHistorySnapshot`
then `recordCharacterHistory`). On origin `develop` `e38ecc710394` it recursed
with `Object.entries`, so a cyclic `content` graph RangeError'd, an enumerable
getter was invoked, and a 20k-deep nest that `JSON.parse` already accepted
(~40 KiB) then stack-overflowed the history walk. Zod `contentSchema` is
`.passthrough()`, so extra keys are not schema-bounded.

Independent origin proof:

```text
origin develop e38ecc710394
honest messageExamples: ok 0ms
zod honest: success=true
JSON.parse extra-arr 20000 (40090 bytes): ok
zod extra-arr 20000: success=true
history extra-arr 20000: THROW 1ms RangeError Maximum call stack size exceeded
zod extra-obj 20000: success=true
history extra-obj 20000: THROW 4ms RangeError
history cyclic content: THROW 12ms RangeError
```

This head walks with descriptor-only reads, a depth/node/cycle budget, and
throws typed `CharacterHistoryError` `CHARACTER_HISTORY_UNBOUNDED` instead
of RangeError. `PUT /api/character` returns 400. Honest snapshots are
unchanged.

Occupancy-FREE hosts `packages/agent/src/services/character-history.ts` and
`packages/agent/src/api/character-routes.ts`
(`scannedAt=2026-08-20T21:45:09.712Z`). Agent leftover. Not a twin of #23127
`agent-export.ts`, #23123 `server-helpers-config.ts`, or #23115
`server-config-filter.ts`. Not leftover-tax of #23034 config-routes nest
rejection or #23054 skill-items YAML. Not a ReDoS twin of #23085 / #23076.
Not a cloud JSON 500 reprint. Not HARD_SKIP `server.ts`.

## What kind of change is this?

Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)

## Why are we doing this? Any context or related work?

`PUT /api/character` validates with Zod, then snapshots `messageExamples`
for persistence and the history journal. `contentSchema.passthrough()` keeps
attacker-controlled extra keys that `JSON.parse` already accepted. A legal
20k-deep nest or cyclic graph then RangeErrors the walk and 500s the route.
Fail-closed before the stack overflows.

## What

Adds `GoogleMapsAdapter` to `@elizaos/plugin-maps`: a real Google Places API (New) + Routes API integration behind the existing `MapsProviderAdapter` seam, with Cloud-managed credentials and a documented local API-key mode.

- **Two explicit credential modes, no silent fallback.** `api-key` mode calls the public Google origins directly with a server-side key in `X-Goog-Api-Key`. `managed` mode calls the Cloud maps gateway under `/google-maps/places/*` and `/google-maps/routes/*` with an opaque session bearer token plus the opaque `conn_…` connection id — no Google key ever exists in the runtime, and endpoint overrides are rejected in managed mode. Browser/server key separation is structural: the runtime key path only exists in server-side `api-key` mode and the key never appears in URLs, contexts, or diagnostics.
- **Validated normalization + attribution.** Google payloads (`places:searchText`, place details with `X-Goog-FieldMask`, `directions/v2:computeRoutes`) are schema-validated and normalized into the plugin's strict `PlaceRef`/`RoutePlan` contracts with a new optional `attribution` field, always set to `Google`. Proto3 zero-omission (`distanceMeters`) is decoded faithfully; `duration: "900s"` strings are parsed; a missing route is a typed `MAPS_NOT_FOUND`.
- **Quotas and costs are explicit.** Optional `maxRequests` budget throws `MAPS_BUDGET_EXHAUSTED` (new typed code) *before* dispatch — budget failure is loud, never a degrade. `usage()` reports per-billed-operation counts, cache hits, and remaining budget.
- **Caching within Google policy.** Place-detail cache TTL is capped at 30 days (default 24h), entry-bounded, and concurrent detail reads for one place ID coalesce into a single upstream call.
- **Shared transport extraction.** The bounded SSRF-guarded read machinery (deadline, teardown, retry-after, byte-limited UTF-8 reads) moved from `JsonMapsHttpAdapter` into `src/transport.ts` so both adapters classify untrusted bytes identically instead of duplicating ~200 lines.

## Tests

`plugins/plugin-maps/test/google-adapter.test.ts` drives the **real adapter** against the repository's protocol-faithful fake provider (`@elizaos/cloud-test-mocks/provider-contract`) in both modes, including the full `outbound-http` conformance profile (14 scenarios): success, designed-empty, invalid input, pagination (pageToken forwarding + pageSize clamp), 429 retry-after metadata, malformed JSON, schema drift, timeout, connection reset, 4xx/5xx, opaque connection id, secret redaction, read policy — plus expired vs revoked auth (Google `UNAUTHENTICATED`/`PERMISSION_DENIED` and gateway `credential_expired`/`credential_revoked`), route not-found, coordinate waypoints, cache/coalescing concurrency, budget exhaustion (no request dispatched), managed-path routing and header separation (bearer + connection id, never an API key), constructor SSRF/endpoint validation, and end-to-end `MapsService` registration.

# Background

# Risks

Medium. This changes workflow execution state and adds a nullable indexed database
column. A crash after a non-transactional external side effect can still leave a
`running` reservation; this PR deliberately reports that state instead of
overclaiming exactly-once execution. The one-time legacy backfill takes a write-
blocking lock on `life_workflow_runs`; deployment must quiesce pre-column workflow
writers before the cutover.

# Background

## What does this PR do?

- Reserves keyed workflow runs with an atomic SQL `INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO
  NOTHING RETURNING` before the first step, then finalizes the winning row with a
  compare-and-set update.
- Replaces the unbounded replay history scan with an indexed point lookup scoped
  by captured `(agentId, workflowId, idempotencyKey)` and distinguishes success,
  failure, partial-compensation failure, cancellation, and in-progress replay.
- Adds the caller-visible `failed_uncompensated` state and a typed error, continues
  reverse compensation after individual compensation failures, and reports each
  failure through `runtime.reportError`.
- Backfills valid legacy keys in bounded keyset pages, deterministically repairs
  duplicates, serializes the cutover under a table lock, and creates the partial
  unique index only after repair.
- Prevents schedule/event cursors and nudges from advancing while the matching
  claimed run remains in progress.

## What kind of change is this?

Bug fix (non-breaking workflow-run persistence and error-contract correction).

# Documentation changes needed?

No public documentation change is needed. The operational cutover constraint and
crash/lease limitation are documented next to the migration and in Deploy Notes.

## What

Builds the visible, policy-controlled browser session UI on top of what is on `develop` today (the `/api/browser-bridge` sessions/settings/confirm routes and the plugin-browser policy helpers):

- **`BrowserSessionPolicyPanel`** (`packages/ui/src/components/browser/BrowserSessionPolicyPanel.tsx`) — lists the agent's bridge sessions with:
  - the effective **domain-mode verdict** per session domain (granted / blocked / all-sites / current-site-only / outside grants / paused / control off / bridge disabled / unresolved), rendered as an accent (orange) or danger badge;
  - **user takeover**: approve/decline controls for `awaiting_confirmation` sessions via `POST /api/browser-bridge/sessions/:id/confirm`;
  - **domain modes**: per-domain grant / block / unblock controls writing `grantedOrigins`/`blockedOrigins` via `POST /api/browser-bridge/settings`;
  - **submit interception**: sessions surface their held steps (explicit `requiresConfirmation`, and account-affecting/submit steps when `requireConfirmationForAccountAffecting` is on);
  - **session TTL**: finished sessions show their retention deadline and are hidden once expired (24h default);
  - **receipts**: finished sessions render their result as a receipt with unconditional redaction of credential-looking keys (token/secret/password/cookie/authorization/…) — no cookie export, no rehosting, ever.
  - Loading, designed-empty, and error are three distinct states with a retry affordance; the clock lives in an effect (never read in render) so renders stay deterministic.
- **`browser-session-policy.ts`** — pure policy math: fail-closed domain-mode resolution ordering (disabled → paused → blocklist → allow modes), origin normalization (`https://x/*`, `*.x`, ports/paths) and subdomain matching, interception selection, TTL expiry, receipt redaction/truncation.
- **`client-browser-bridge.ts`** — typed `ElizaClient` extension over the existing bridge routes (`listBrowserBridgeSessions`, `getBrowserBridgeSettings`, `updateBrowserBridgeSettings`, `confirmBrowserBridgeSession`), registered in `api/client.ts`.
- Storybook stories for empty / load-error / awaiting-takeover / blocked+outside-grants / finished-with-receipt states (story-gate coverage).

## Tests

- `browser-session-policy.test.ts` — 16 deterministic unit tests: disabled/paused pre-emption, blocklist-beats-all_sites, granted vs outside grants, subdomain vs suffix-fragment matching, unresolved-domain fail-closed, interception on/off, TTL anchor (finishedAt vs updatedAt), bad-timestamp tolerance, redaction (including nested objects) and truncation.
- `BrowserSessionPolicyPanel.test.tsx` — 8 jsdom behaviour tests driven through a protocol-faithful in-memory transport (confirm flips awaiting→queued/cancelled; settings writes merge like the route): loading→empty, error→retry→ready, per-domain verdict rendering, approve and decline takeover, grant then block a domain, intercepted-step + redacted-receipt rendering (secret value never in DOM), action-error banner on a failed write.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)b2:T10a2,Fixes #19885

## What

Derives — rather than predesigns — the reusable managed-provider adapter SDK from the existing plugin-maps JSON adapter, and lands it in `@elizaos/core` under `src/integrations/managed-provider/` (exported from the root Node surface):

- **Connection resolver** (`connection.ts`): explicit `managed` (opaque `conn_*` Cloud connection id + gateway origin, no credential ever present at the runtime) vs `local`/BYO (explicit endpoint + user credential) modes. Strict validation of provider ids, opaque connection ids, and origin-only endpoints; **no silent fallback** between modes. Local connections get a deterministic opaque audit handle that never embeds the endpoint or credential.
- **Typed HTTP client** (`http-client.ts`): SSRF-guarded (core `fetchWithSsrfGuard`, DNS-pinned, redirects rejected), origin-pinned, deadline-bounded, byte-limited JSON transport with schema-validated decoding (structural `safeParse` seam, no zod dependency in core) and a designed-null 404 path (`requestOptionalJson`).
- **Failure taxonomy** (`errors.ts`): `ManagedProviderError` with stable codes (auth expired/revoked, rate limited + `retryAfterMs`, timeout, network, endpoint blocked, oversize, malformed, rejected/failure, pagination overflow) and `toCapabilityExecutionErrorCode` mapping onto the #19878 capability execution contract.
- **Pagination** (`pagination.ts`): `collectProviderPages` with page/item ceilings and repeated/empty-cursor rejection so a hostile upstream cannot loop the runtime.
- **Health** (`health.ts`): non-throwing `probeProviderHealth` producing typed snapshots (`healthy` / `reauth_required` / `revoked` / `rate_limited` / `unreachable` / `degraded`) for catalog/kill-switch and Connections surfaces (#19887/#19884).

## Reference migration

`plugins/plugin-maps/src/adapter.ts` is rewritten on top of the SDK (−580/+120 lines of transport code): the SDK owns transport, deadlines, bounded reads, and classification; the plugin keeps the maps route contract, provider-spoofing assertions, and translates the shared taxonomy into `MapsError` codes at its boundary. Managed mode (no credential) and local/BYO mode (credential) both go through `resolveProviderConnection`. The plugin's full existing suite — including `test/provider-contract.test.ts`, which drives the real HTTP adapter against the #19909 protocol-faithful fake upstream — passes unchanged, proving behavior parity. Local mode has no runtime Cloud dependency; the SDK lives in `@elizaos/core` (ESM, project references).

## Tests

- New deterministic suite `packages/core/src/integrations/managed-provider/managed-provider.test.ts` (17 tests) over injected transports: success, designed-empty and designed-null, invalid input (ids/endpoints/limits), pagination (drain, loops, overflows), expired/revoked auth, rate limiting with retry-after, malformed/contract-drift/oversize bodies without leaking provider bytes, timeouts, private/blocked origin rejection, bearer/connection-id header propagation.
- `bun run --cwd packages/core test -- src/integrations/managed-provider` — 17 passed.

## What

Adds a provider-neutral normalized finance capability layer to `@elizaos/plugin-finances`, with freshness/calculation metadata on reads and receipts on internal writes. Read/derive only — nothing implies payments or trading.

**New module `src/finance-capabilities.ts`** (pure, deterministic, no I/O):
- `computeSourceBalances` — per-source ledger-derived net flow (credits minus settled debits). Pending rows are excluded from settled figures and reported separately; every observed currency is surfaced instead of silently merged; metadata explicitly states balances are transaction-derived, not institution-reported.
- `computeBudgetStatus` — user-supplied budget vs settled debit spend in a rolling window (`under_budget` / `near_limit` / `over_budget`), with pending/credit/out-of-window rows excluded and counted.
- `detectAnomalies` — possible duplicate charges (same source/merchant/amount within 3 days) and amount spikes (>= 2.5x a merchant's average over 3+ prior charges, >= $20 delta). Uses the normalized merchant name so adversarial raw strings ("NETFLlX.COM*8873") group with their real merchant; pending rows never generate anomalies.
- `normalizeSubscriptions` — regular-cadence recurring charges (confidence >= 0.5) projected into provider-neutral subscription records.
- `buildCapabilityMeta` — `FinanceCapabilityMeta` on every capability response: `generatedAt`, freshness (`latestDataAt` of consumed rows, counts), and calculation provenance (`derived_from_transactions` | `provider_reported` | `user_supplied_input`, window, notes).
- `buildWriteReceipt` — `FinanceWriteReceipt` (id, capability, operation, entity, occurredAt, outcome, counts) with no credentials or row payloads.

**Action surface (`src/actions/finances.ts`)**: four new OWNER_FINANCES subactions — `balances`, `budget_status` (requires `budgetUsd`, rejects missing/non-positive), `subscriptions`, `anomalies` — and receipts attached to the existing internal writes (`add_source`, `remove_source`, `import_csv`; the CSV receipt is only issued when state actually changed). All exported from the package barrel; docs (CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md/README) updated.

## Tests

- `src/finance-capabilities.test.ts` — 17 deterministic unit tests over the pure layer: multi-account, multi-currency, pending rows, duplicate/near-duplicate/cross-source negatives, adversarial merchant strings, thin-history spike suppression, empty ledgers, receipt shape/uniqueness, strict pending-flag typing.
- `test/finances.real-db.test.ts` — 4 new real-PGLite integration tests driving `runPaymentsHandler` end to end: write receipts on add/remove source, derived balances + freshness metadata from real rows, budget_status invalid-input + over-budget evaluation, and a real duplicate-charge anomaly plus designed-empty subscriptions.

## What this does

Projects all managed connections into the shared connected-capability API without merging their storage tables, on top of the provider-neutral `ConnectedAccount` contract merged for #19878 (PR #22643).

- **Projection service** (`packages/cloud/shared/src/lib/services/connected-capabilities/`): maps four storage families — cloud OAuth credentials (`platform_credentials`), vendor OAuth connections (`vendor_connections`), Discord connector accounts (`discord_connections`), and native phone-gateway devices (`phone_gateway_devices`) — into contract-normalized `ConnectedAccount` DTOs via the real `normalizeConnectedAccount` from `@elizaos/core`. Storage tables stay separate; the DB loader reads each with an org-scoped SQL filter.
- **Opaque handles, no secrets**: account IDs are `ca_<sha256-derived>` digests of source family + row ID — never credential row IDs. The projection never reads token/ciphertext/DEK/nonce columns; tests assert the serialized payload contains no secret material, email, phone number, or row UUID.
- **Status / last-used / capabilities**: credential lifecycle states map onto contract statuses (`connected`, `reauth_required`, `revoked`, `error`, `disabled`, `unavailable`); granted OAuth scopes project to per-capability risk levels (mutating scopes R2, reads R1); phone-gateway native permission booleans project as capabilities, with ungranted permissions surfaced as `unsupported` rather than hidden.
- **API**: `GET /api/v1/connections/accounts` (offset pagination via the shared fail-closed parser, `providerId`/`mode` filters) and `GET /api/v1/connections/accounts/:accountId` (detail; cross-org and unknown handles 404, malformed handles 400). Mounted ahead of the legacy `/connections/:platform` param route.
- **Worker bundle**: the Workers `@elizaos/core` shim re-exports the pure provider-integration contract pieces from real core source so the Worker runs the actual normalizer, not a stub.
- **Cloud SDK**: regenerated public-route surface adds `getApiV1ConnectionsAccounts` / `getApiV1ConnectionsAccountsByAccountId`, plus mirrored `ConnectedAccount*Dto` types.

## Scope notes

- Local/self-hosted BYO-credential runtimes have no cloud-persisted connection state today; the contract's `local` mode is already served by the enum and the projection's source-loader seam, so a local source registers without an API change when one lands (per the #19877 architecture, local mode never silently falls back to Cloud).
- Rate limiting rides the API-wide middleware; the routes add no per-route override.

## Tests and gates

- `packages/cloud/shared` — 13 new deterministic contract tests over the real projection/service (success, designed-empty, revoked/error/reauth, malformed upstream scopes, soft deletes, pagination totals, cross-org handle isolation, handle stability, fail-closed loader): **13 pass**.
- `packages/cloud/api` — 10 new Hono route tests running the live handlers against a real `ConnectedCapabilitiesService` over typed rows (defaults, pagination, invalid limit/offset/provider/mode, provider filter, empty org, 401, structured 500 without storage context, detail 200/404/400): **10 pass**.
- `packages/cloud/sdk` — full package tests: 195 pass; typecheck clean.

# Risks

**Low, with two deliberate behaviour changes.**

- Below the budgets nothing changes — proven byte-for-byte across a 38-case
  origin-vs-branch corpus covering both directions (status, refund decision,
  **and** the full body text).
- A caller request body over **1,000,000 bytes** now gets a typed `413` with the
  pre-charge refunded, where it previously succeeded at unbounded memory cost.
- An MCP response body over **5,000,000 bytes** now gets a typed `502` with the
  pre-charge refunded, where it previously succeeded, **was billed**, and was
  returned to the caller in full.
- Both ceilings are two constants derived from one number
  (`MAX_PROXY_REQUEST_BODY_BYTES` and a `x5` multiplier), copied from
  `services/oauth/credential-broker.ts`. If a maintainer wants different numbers
  for MCP specifically, that is a one-line change and I would rather be told than
  guess.
- Over-budget is never a truncated body served as success. The read is abandoned
  and the money is given back.

# Background

## What does this PR do?

`POST /api/mcp/proxy/:mcpId` buffers two bodies into the isolate with no byte
budget on either (`packages/cloud/api/mcp/proxy/[mcpId]/route.ts` on
`origin/develop`):

```
:126  export async function parseJsonBody(request: Request) {
:131    const text = await request.text();          <- caller's body, unbounded
...
:436  try {
:437    responseBody = await mcpResponse.text();    <- MCP's body, unbounded
```

The second one is the sharp end. `mcpResponse` comes from
`safeFetch(targetUrl, …)` where `targetUrl` is `mcp.external_endpoint` — a URL
the MCP's owner chose. `safeFetch` validates the target and pins the resolved
IP, which is the right SSRF guard; it has **no size cap and no deadline**. So
the number of bytes one proxied call spends inside the isolate is chosen by
whoever registered the MCP.

`:437` is not the last copy either: the string is handed to
`isJsonRpcErrorResponse()` (`:97`), which `JSON.parse`s the whole thing again
when it looks like an envelope, and then to `new Response(responseBody, …)`.

This package deploys as a Cloudflare Worker
(`packages/cloud/api/wrangler.toml`, `name = "eliza-cloud-api"`), where
per-isolate memory is a hard platform limit.

**On the existing protection, precisely.** Both reads *are* inside `try`/`catch`
and both catches are real — `refundPrecharge("mcp_response_read_failed")` then a
`502`. That handles a read *failure*: a reset socket, a decode error. It cannot
help here, because **there is no failure to catch — the read succeeds**. And
even if it threw, a `catch` runs after the allocation it would like to prevent.
The pre-charge/refund ledger around the call is correct and orthogonal: it
decides who pays, not how much memory is spent.

**Reachability.** `requireUserOrApiKeyWithOrg(c)` — any authenticated user with
an active organization. `resolveMcpProxyView` (`:115`) grants access to the
owner of an MCP *or* to any caller when the MCP `is_public`. A caller therefore
needs one MCP: a public one someone else registered, or one they registered
themselves pointed at a host they control — in which case the response size is
entirely their own choice.

## What kind of change is this?

Bug fix (non-breaking, except as stated under **Risks**).

## The fix

A new import-free module,
`packages/cloud/api/mcp/proxy/[mcpId]/proxy-body-budget.ts`, exporting
`readBodyTextWithinBudget(source, maxBytes, onCancelFailure?)`. It charges the
budget **before** the bytes are retained, in two stages:

1. a declared `content-length` over budget is refused **without reading the body
   at all**, and the body is cancelled best-effort;
2. otherwise the body is streamed and each chunk is charged against the running
   total **before** it is retained, so peak retention is the budget plus the
   chunk in hand. Decoding is incremental (`TextDecoder(…, { stream: true })`),
   so the raw bytes are not held alongside the finished string. A
   `content-length` that is absent, non-numeric, or not a safe integer is **not**
   treated as a budget grant.

The two ceilings are lifted from
`packages/cloud/shared/src/lib/services/oauth/credential-broker.ts` — the
platform's other "proxy one call to a caller-supplied host" service — and
derived the same way (#23900):

```ts
const MAX_PROXY_REQUEST_BODY_BYTES = 1_000_000;
const PROXY_RESPONSE_BODY_BUDGET_MULTIPLIER = 5;
const MAX_PROXY_RESPONSE_BODY_BYTES =
  MAX_PROXY_REQUEST_BODY_BYTES * PROXY_RESPONSE_BODY_BUDGET_MULTIPLIER;
```

so moving the request cap moves both. Over-budget refunds the pre-charge and
returns a typed `413` (request) or `502` (response), reusing the route's existing
`refundPrecharge(reason, metadata)` ledger with two new reasons,
`request_body_too_large` and `mcp_response_too_large`.

`parseJsonBody` keeps its exported signature and gains an optional `maxBytes`
that defaults to the request budget, so its existing unit tests in
`packages/cloud/api/__tests__/mcp-proxy-helpers.test.ts` continue to call it
exactly as before. The non-JSON `content-type` short-circuit still returns `{}`
without reading the body at all.

# Documentation changes needed?

My changes do not require a change to the project documentation.

## Detailed testing steps

### 1. Allocation, origin vs branch, through the production seam

`safeFetch` returns a real WHATWG `Response`, so the production seam is
`Response.text()` on that object. The driver builds a real `Response` over a real
`ReadableStream` emitting 1 MiB chunks and samples `process.memoryUsage()` at
the instant the read resolves. Same 256 MiB upstream in every row:

| | declared `content-length` | RSS at read complete | `arrayBuffers` | heapUsed | outcome |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `origin/develop` | yes | **+776.5 MiB** | +256.0 MiB | +190.3 MiB | `200`, **billed**, 268,435,456-char body |
| `origin/develop` | no | **+777.2 MiB** | +256.0 MiB | +190.3 MiB | `200`, **billed** |
| `origin/develop`, real JSON envelope | no | **+776.6 MiB** | +256.0 MiB | +190.3 MiB | `200`, **billed** |
| this branch | yes | **+5.1 MiB** | +0.0 MiB | +0.0 MiB | `502`, refunded |
| this branch | no | **+14.0 MiB** | +0.0 MiB | +0.0 MiB | `502`, refunded |
| this branch, real JSON envelope | no | **+14.1 MiB** | +0.0 MiB | +0.0 MiB | `502`, refunded |

Note the outcome column on `develop`: this is not a request that fails
expensively — it **succeeds**, bills, and returns a quarter-gigabyte body.

### 2. No over-rejection — 38 cases, both directions, origin vs branch identical

Every case is traffic that succeeds on `develop` today. For each, two identical
real WHATWG objects are built and one is run through each sequence; status,
refund decision **and** the full body text are compared.

- Responses (each declared and chunked): empty, whitespace-only, a JSON-RPC
  `result`, a JSON-RPC `error` envelope (must still refund), an all-error batch,
  a partial-success batch (must still bill), non-JSON, malformed JSON, multi-byte
  UTF-8 repeated across chunk boundaries, a 900 KB result, a 4 MB result, and a
  body sized to the budget exactly.
- Requests (each declared and chunked): empty JSON body, a normal `tools/call`,
  multi-byte arguments, 900 KB of arguments, a non-JSON `content-type`, no
  `content-type` at all, and malformed JSON (must still throw `SyntaxError`).

```
corpus: 38 cases, identical=38, divergent=0
```

The multi-byte cases matter specifically: they prove the incremental
`TextDecoder` never splits a UTF-8 sequence across a chunk boundary.

### 3. Load-bearing revert, by copy-aside (not `git stash`)

The new module was copied aside and only the budget was neutralized inside it
(`maxBytes = Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY`), leaving the restructured read intact.
The 256 MiB response went straight back to `200` **billed** at +634.6 MiB RSS.
Restoring the file restored the `502` at +14.0 MiB.

### 4. Typecheck

The new module compiles clean under the package's own strict compiler settings,
TypeScript 6.0.3, zero diagnostics.

## Known gaps / failures

- **`bun run verify` was not run, and neither was the `packages/cloud` package
  typecheck nor `packages/cloud/api/__tests__`** (including the existing
  `mcp-proxy-refund.test.ts` and `mcp-proxy-helpers.test.ts`, which drive this
  route). This machine could not complete a workspace install: the checkout
  lives on an external volume measured at ~1.6 MB/s under concurrent load, and
  `bun install` did not finish. Everything above was produced without
  `node_modules` by driving the real new module — deliberately import-free for
  exactly this reason — under `bun`. The package typecheck against an untouched
  control and the two existing MCP-proxy suites are **not** run here and are the
  gap a reviewer should close. `parseJsonBody`'s signature was kept
  backward-compatible specifically so those suites keep passing unmodified, but
  that is reasoning, not a green run.
- **No new test file is added**, for the same reason: a `__tests__` entry that
  has never been executed would be a claim, not evidence. I will add cases to
  `mcp-proxy-refund.test.ts` in this PR if a maintainer prefers that to merging
  the fix first.
- **Node/bun `Response` is not workerd.** The absolute MiB figures would differ
  on workerd; the *shape* — whole body materialized before any check on
  `develop`, not materialized on this branch — is a property of the code, not the
  runtime.
- **The hop is still un-deadlined.** Neither the `safeFetch` call nor the
  container-endpoint `fetch` carries an `AbortSignal`, so a slow MCP can hold the
  isolate for as long as the platform allows. That is a different mechanism (time,
  not bytes) with a different fix and it is deliberately not folded in here;
  #24050 records this PR's scope as the byte budgets.
- **No rate limit or per-key concurrency cap is added.** Nothing bounds how many
  proxied MCP calls one API key may make; this bounds the cost of each one.
- **Hosted CI checks do not run on this PR.** I contribute from a fork without
  push access to `elizaOS/eliza`, so no hosted check will report here, and
  nothing above should be read as "CI passed".
